market-structure-shift-mss-screener.title: Market Structure Shift (MSS) Screener
market-structure-shift-mss-screener.summary: Marks the bar where price closes through the middle of the last three swings against the prevailing structure, boxes the swing range and lists recent shifts in a table.
market-structure-shift-mss-screener.descriptionHtml:
The study builds a zig zag from swing points. A bar is a swing high when its high is the highest of the last Zig Zag Length bars, and a swing low when its low is the lowest (or the body extremes, with the Open/Close source). A new pivot starts each time the swing direction turns, and the newest pivot moves on while price keeps extending it. From the newest five pivots the study reads three swings: the second, third and fourth newest, so the leg that is still forming is left out once five pivots exist.

A bearish market structure shift needs the newest of the three swings to be the highest, the middle one the lowest and the oldest in between, and a close on a finished bar that crosses below the middle swing while sitting below all three. A bullish shift is the mirror image. Each shift must also pass the displacement filter: by default the newest swing must sit more than Percentage Above percent away from the oldest one, or, with the Multiplier filter, the newest leg must be that many times the previous leg.

On a shift the study shades a box over the swing range, draws a dashed line along the broken middle swing to the shift bar and colours the candle. It then holds a level one third of the way back into the broken range. When the high next crosses up through the bearish level, or the low crosses down through the bullish one, the retracement is marked with a dotted line back to the swing it was measured from. A table in the corner lists the most recent shifts or retracements on this instrument, with the bar time, the close and the side.
market-structure-shift-mss-screener.howToReadHtml:
A pink down triangle above a candle is a bearish shift: the market made a higher swing, then closed back below the swing low before it, which is read as sellers taking over the recent structure. A teal up triangle below a candle is the bullish version. The box shows the range the shift broke out of, and the dashed line is the level that gave way. A Ret mark and dotted line show price coming back one third of the way into that range, the follow-up entry this method looks for.

The swings are only known once the zig zag has turned, so the newest leg can still move and the signals describe structure that has already formed. On choppy charts small swings produce many shifts; raise the zig zag length or the filter to keep only the larger moves. A shift is a change in recent structure, not a forecast that the move will continue.

settings.label: Screening Method
settings.html: Chooses what the table lists: the structure shift bars themselves, or the bars where price retraced back to the one third level after a shift.

settings.label: Direction
settings.html: Limits the table to bullish rows, bearish rows or both.

settings.label: Only Bullish
settings.html: Despite its label, this switch lets bearish rows into the table: turning it off removes the bearish rows, not the bullish ones.

settings.label: Only Bearish
settings.html: Lets bullish rows into the table. As with the switch above, turning it off removes the bullish rows.

settings.label: Display Rows
settings.html: How many of the most recent signals the table lists, newest first. Zero shows only the two header rows.

settings.label: Table Position
settings.html: Where the table sits. Tables pin to the four corners, so a top row goes to the top, a middle or bottom row to the bottom, a left column to the left and a centre or right column to the right.

settings.label: Table Size
settings.html: Kept for saved settings. Tables in this version draw at the chart's own text size, so this choice changes nothing.

settings.label: Bearish
settings.html: Shows or hides everything bearish: the shift markers, boxes, levels, retracement lines and candle colours.

settings.label: Bearish Shift
settings.html: Shows the bearish shift marker, its candle colour and the dashed broken level. The swing box stays while Bearish is on.

settings.label: Bearish Retracement
settings.html: Shows the bearish retracement mark, its candle colour and the dotted line at the one third level.

settings.label: Bullish
settings.html: Shows or hides everything bullish: the shift markers, boxes, levels, retracement lines and candle colours.

settings.label: Bullish Shift
settings.html: Shows the bullish shift marker, its candle colour and the dashed broken level. The swing box stays while Bullish is on.

settings.label: Bullish Retracement
settings.html: Shows the bullish retracement mark, its candle colour and the dotted line at the one third level.

settings.label: Zig Zag Length
settings.html: A bar is a swing high or low when it is the highest or lowest of this many bars, itself included. A longer length finds fewer, larger swings and fewer shifts.

settings.label: Source
settings.html: Builds swings from the wicks (High/Low) or from the candle bodies (Open/Close), which ignores spikes that closed back inside the body.

settings.label: Show Zig Zag
settings.html: Draws the zig zag line through every pivot, up to the newest 500.

settings.label: Box Transparency
settings.html: How see-through the swing range box is, from 0 solid to 100 invisible.

settings.label: Filter Using
settings.html: Picks the displacement test a shift must pass: a percentage distance between the newest and oldest swing, or a multiple of the previous leg.

settings.label: Multiplier
settings.html: With the Multiplier filter, the newest leg must be more than this many times the previous leg.

settings.label: Percentage Above
settings.html: With the Percentage filter, the newest swing must be more than this percent away from the oldest one. Zero lets every shift through.

faq.q: Why do some shifts have a box but no dashed line?
faq.html: The box is drawn whenever the side is shown, while the dashed broken level follows the Shift switch. Turning off Bearish Shift or Bullish Shift keeps the boxes and removes the markers, levels and candle colours for that side.

faq.q: What is the retracement level?
faq.html: After a shift the study holds a price one third of the way from the newest swing back toward the broken middle swing. The first bar whose high crosses up through the bearish level, or whose low crosses down through the bullish level, is marked once as the retracement.

faq.q: Why does the table only show this instrument?
faq.html: A study runs on the one instrument its chart shows, so the screener reports that instrument's own signals: the bar time, the close rounded to the tick and whether the shift was bullish or bearish.

faq.q: Why are there no signals on my chart?
faq.html: The percentage filter may be too strict for the timeframe. On an hourly chart a 0.7 percent swing is common, but on a five minute chart it can be rare. Lower Percentage Above (0 lets every shift through) or shorten the zig zag length.

market-structure-shift-mss.title: Market Structure Shift (MSS)
market-structure-shift-mss.summary: Marks the close that breaks back through the middle of the last three swings, boxes the swing range it broke, and flags a one-third retracement into it.
market-structure-shift-mss.descriptionHtml:
The study builds a zig zag of swing highs and lows. A bar is a swing high when its high (or the top of its body, with the Open/Close source) is the highest of the last Zig Zag Length bars, and a swing low is the mirror image. A lone swing high turns the direction up and a lone swing low turns it down. On a change of direction a new pivot is added; while the direction holds, a further extreme moves the newest pivot to the new price. The study keeps the newest five pivots and reads three swings from them, counted from the oldest held, so with five pivots they are the second, third and fourth newest.

A bearish shift needs the newest of those three swings to be the highest, the middle one to be the lowest, and the close to sit below all three after crossing down through the middle swing on this bar. A bullish shift is the mirror image. The swing displacement must also clear a filter: either the newest swing leg is more than Multiplier times the one before it, or the move from the oldest swing to the newest is larger than Percentage Above percent of the oldest swing's price.

Each shift sets a retracement level a third of the way back from the newest swing toward the broken middle swing. The first bar, from the shift bar on, whose high crosses up through a bearish level (or whose low crosses down through a bullish one) completes the sequence and is marked as the retracement. A further shift before that moves the level to the new swings. Shifts and retracements are only taken on closed bars.
market-structure-shift-mss.howToReadHtml:
A pink triangle above a candle, with the candle painted pink, is a bearish shift: price has closed back below the swing low that the last push higher started from, which suggests the up move has failed. A green triangle below a green candle is the bullish version. The shaded box runs from the oldest of the three swings to the newest, in both time and price, and the dashed line runs along the broken swing to the shift bar. An R marks the first bar that comes back to the retracement level, one third of the last leg below the newest swing high (above the newest swing low for a bullish shift), which is the follow-up entry the method looks for. A dotted line marks that level.

The newest pivot keeps moving while price extends in its direction, and the three swings are read from the pivots behind it, so a shift is only called once a newer swing has formed and a close has come back through the middle one. A shift can fail and be followed by a shift the other way; a wider filter gives fewer, larger structures. Turn on Show Zig Zag to see the swings the study is reading.

settings.label: Bearish
settings.html: Show everything on the bearish side: shift markers, retracement markers, candle colours, boxes and lines.

settings.label: Bearish Shift
settings.html: Show the bearish shift marker, its candle colour and the dashed line along the broken swing.

settings.label: Bearish Retracement
settings.html: Show the bearish retracement marker, its candle colour and its dotted level.

settings.label: Bullish
settings.html: Show everything on the bullish side: shift markers, retracement markers, candle colours, boxes and lines.

settings.label: Bullish Shift
settings.html: Show the bullish shift marker, its candle colour and the dashed line along the broken swing.

settings.label: Bullish Retracement
settings.html: Show the bullish retracement marker, its candle colour and its dotted level.

settings.label: Zig Zag Length
settings.html: How many bars a swing high or low must top or undercut. Larger values find fewer, wider swings.

settings.label: Source
settings.html: High/Low reads the candle's wicks for the swings; Open/Close reads the top and bottom of its body.

settings.label: Show Zig Zag
settings.html: Draw the path through every swing pivot the study has found, up to the newest 500.

settings.label: Box Transparency
settings.html: How faint the swing range box is: 0 is solid and 100 is invisible.

settings.label: Filter Using
settings.html: Multiplier compares the newest swing leg with the one before it; Percentage compares the move with the price of the oldest swing.

settings.label: Multiplier
settings.html: With the Multiplier filter, how many times larger the newest swing leg must be than the previous one.

settings.label: Percentage Above
settings.html: With the Percentage filter, the smallest move from the oldest to the newest swing, as a percentage of the oldest swing's price. 0 turns the filter off.

faq.q: Why does a shift appear several bars after the swing it breaks?
faq.html: A shift needs three swings plus the later close through the middle one. With five pivots held, those three are the second, third and fourth newest, so a newer swing has to form first. The marker sits on the bar where the close came back through.

faq.q: What does the R marker mean?
faq.html: It is the first bar after a shift that trades back to the level one third of the last swing leg short of the newest swing. At most one R follows a shift, and a further shift before it arrives replaces the level. The dotted line runs from the newest swing to the R bar at that level.

faq.q: Why do I see fewer shifts on the Percentage filter?
faq.html: The default 0.7 percent asks for a move of 0.7 percent of the oldest swing's price, which removes the narrow structures. Set it to 0 to take every shift the swing pattern allows.

mitigation-block-scanner.title: Mitigation Block Scanner
mitigation-block-scanner.summary: Finds the nine-pivot swing pattern of a mitigation block on a zig zag and marks the bar where the close breaks through it, or the later retest of that level.
mitigation-block-scanner.descriptionHtml:
The study builds a zig zag from swing extremes. A bar is a swing high when its high is the highest of the last Zig Zag Length bars, and a swing low when its low is the lowest. A new swing in the opposite direction starts a new pivot, and a further extreme in the same direction moves the newest pivot rather than adding one. The source of the swings can be the high and low, the larger of open and close, or the close alone.

On every bar the newest nine pivots are compared with each other. A short setup is an advance that tops out: the swings rise to a peak, then price makes a lower high, a low below the previous swing low, and another lower high, while the newest swing is still forming. A long setup is the mirror image. When that shape is in place and the close crosses the price of that last swing low (or, for a long, the last swing high), the bar is a shift. The study draws a box over the whole structure, a dashed line at the broken pivot's price, colours the candle and marks the bar.

The Retracement method uses the same shift to arm the broken level, then waits for price to come back to it: for a short, the first bar whose high rises above the level after the previous high stayed below it. That bar is marked, coloured and joined to the level with a dotted line. A set of optional filters (day change, day volume, volume change, ATR, body size, volume average, relative volume, time of day and date) can hold back signals. A small table on the newest bar shows the day's percentage change, the day's volume change, the day's volume and the previous day's volume.
mitigation-block-scanner.howToReadHtml:
A pale red triangle above a bar is a bearish shift: the swing structure turned down and the close broke below its last swing low. A pale green triangle below a bar is the bullish shift. The shaded box shows the swings that formed the pattern, and the dashed line marks the level that was broken. With the Retracement method, an arrow marks the bar where price comes back to that level instead of the break, and a dotted line joins it to the level.

The pattern is strict, so signals are rare, and the zig zag only knows a pivot is final when price swings the other way, so the newest segment can still move. A shift is a description of structure, not a forecast: it can fail, and the filters only narrow the bars where it is allowed to fire.

settings.label: Screening Method
settings.html: Mitigation Block marks the shift bar itself. Retracement marks the later bar where price returns to the level the shift broke.

settings.label: Long Signals
settings.html: Show the bullish shifts or retracements, with their boxes, lines, markers and candle colours.

settings.label: Short Signals
settings.html: Show the bearish shifts or retracements, with their boxes, lines, markers and candle colours.

settings.label: Display Zig Zag
settings.html: Draw the zig zag that joins the pivots. The pattern is still read when the line is hidden.

settings.label: Zig Zag Length
settings.html: The window, in bars, that a swing high must be the highest of and a swing low the lowest of. A longer length gives fewer, larger swings.

settings.label: Source
settings.html: What the swings are measured on: the high and low, the larger of open and close, or the close.

settings.label: Box Transparency
settings.html: Transparency of the structure box, from 0 for solid to 100 for invisible.

settings.label: Apply % Change Filter
settings.html: Requires the day's change to be both above the positive and below the negative threshold at once. No bar can meet both, so switching it on suppresses every signal.

settings.label: % Change Above/Below +/-
settings.html: The day change threshold, in percent, used by the % change filter.

settings.label: Apply Volume Filter
settings.html: Only allow signals while the day's running volume is at least the Volume Above value.

settings.label: Volume Above
settings.html: The day volume the volume filter requires. The first day on the chart has no running total, so it never passes.

settings.label: Apply Volume % Change Filter
settings.html: Only allow signals while the day's running volume is up by at least the given percentage on the previous day's total.

settings.label: Volume % Change Above
settings.html: The volume change, in percent against the previous day, that the volume change filter requires.

settings.label: Apply ATR Filter
settings.html: Only allow signals on bars whose high to low range is wider than the ATR times the multiplier.

settings.label: ATR Length
settings.html: The number of bars in the average true range used by the ATR filter.

settings.label: ATR Multiplier
settings.html: How many ATRs wide a bar must be to pass the ATR filter.

settings.label: Apply Body % Filter
settings.html: Only allow signals on bars whose body is at least the given share of the bar's range.

settings.label: Body % Above
settings.html: The body as a percentage of the range that the body filters require. A bar with no range fails.

settings.label: Apply Body Size Filter
settings.html: Requires the body test above and a range at least the multiplier times the previous bar's range.

settings.label: Body Size Multiplier (x)
settings.html: How many times the previous bar's range this bar's range must be to pass the body size filter.

settings.label: Apply Volume SMA Filter
settings.html: Only allow signals on bars whose volume is above its simple moving average.

settings.label: Volume SMA Length
settings.html: The number of bars in the volume average used by the volume SMA filter.

settings.label: Apply Relative Volume Filter
settings.html: Only allow signals when relative volume, this bar's volume over the previous bar's volume average, is above its own average times the multiplier.

settings.label: Relative Volume Length
settings.html: The number of bars in both the volume average and the relative volume average.

settings.label: Rel Vol SMA Multiplier
settings.html: How many times its own average the relative volume must be to pass the filter.

settings.label: Apply Time Filter
settings.html: Only allow signals on bars that open inside the time window, in the chart's timezone.

settings.label: Time From (hour)
settings.html: The hour the time window opens, compared with the time each bar opens.

settings.label: Time From (minute)
settings.html: The minute the time window opens. A bar opening at this minute is inside the window.

settings.label: Time To (hour)
settings.html: The hour the time window closes.

settings.label: Time To (minute)
settings.html: The minute the time window closes. A bar opening at this minute is already outside it.

settings.label: Apply Date Filter
settings.html: Only allow signals on bars of one calendar date, in the chart's timezone.

settings.label: Day
settings.html: The day of the month the date filter accepts.

settings.label: Month
settings.html: The month, 1 to 12, the date filter accepts.

settings.label: Year
settings.html: The year the date filter accepts.

settings.label: Display Table
settings.html: Show the panel with the day's change, the day's volume change, the day's volume and the previous day's volume.

settings.label: Position
settings.html: Where the panel sits. Panels pin to the four corners, so a top position goes to the top and a middle or bottom one to the bottom, on the left for a left position and on the right otherwise.

settings.label: Size
settings.html: The panel's text size. Tables in this version draw at the chart's own text size, so changing it has no visible effect.

faq.q: Why are there so few signals?
faq.html: The short and long setups each test more than twenty relations between the newest nine pivots, and the close must then cross the pattern's last swing low or high on that very bar. On two months of hourly bars the default settings mark only about a dozen bars. Changing the Zig Zag Length changes which swings count as pivots, and so which bars qualify; a shorter length does not always give more signals.

faq.q: What is the difference between the two methods?
faq.html: Mitigation Block marks the bar where the close breaks the level, with a box over the structure and a dashed line at the level. Retracement keeps the same boxes but marks the later bar where price comes back to the broken level, joined to it by a dotted line. The retracement only counts the first return after each shift.

faq.q: Why does switching on the % change filter remove every signal?
faq.html: That filter requires the day's change to be above the positive threshold and below the negative threshold on the same bar, which cannot happen. The study keeps the test exactly as it is defined, so leave it off unless you want to silence the signals.

faq.q: Why does the newest part of the zig zag move?
faq.html: A pivot is only final once price swings the other way by the Zig Zag Length rule. Until then, a further high in an up leg or a further low in a down leg moves the newest pivot, and its segment follows it. Signals are only taken on closed bars.

retracement-to-order-block-with-screener.title: Retracement to Order Block with Screener
retracement-to-order-block-with-screener.summary: Marks an order block in three steps: a range-breaking momentum candle, a close beyond it, and the retracement back to its level, with a table of recent entries.
retracement-to-order-block-with-screener.descriptionHtml:
The study looks for an order block in three numbered steps. Signal 1 is a momentum candle: its body is more than 66 percent of its range, its range is at least one 14-bar ATR (average true range), and it breaks the range of the previous Period candles. A bearish candle that makes a new low below the lowest low marks a long setup; a bullish candle that makes a new high above the highest high marks a short setup. Only the first such candle after the side changes counts.

Signal 2 is a later candle of the opposite colour that closes beyond the first candle: above its high for a long, below its low for a short, again with a range of at least one ATR. Signal 3 is the entry: after signal 2, price crosses back into the order block level, which is the first candle's high for a long or its low for a short. Vertical Offset pushes that level out by a share of the first candle's range, so price need not touch it exactly.

Each step is marked with a small numbered circle, below the candle for a long and above it for a short. A line is drawn from the newest first candle at its high or low and extended to the right, and a table lists the most recent third signals with their time, side and close.
retracement-to-order-block-with-screener.howToReadHtml:
Read the numbers as a sequence. A 1 shows a strong candle that swept the recent range, a 2 shows price closing back through that candle, and a 3 shows price returning to the level the first candle left behind, which is where the setup expects an entry. A 3 never appears without a 1 and a 2 before it on the same side: each step waits for the step before it.

The extended line keeps the newest order block level on screen, and the table gives a quick list of the latest entries. The signals use only closed bars and fixed rules, so they say nothing about the size of the move that follows; a level that price cuts straight through is not a defended level.

settings.label: Period
settings.html: How many earlier candles the first candle must break the high or low of. A longer period asks for a larger sweep and gives fewer setups.

settings.label: Vertical Offset (%)
settings.html: Pushes the order block level out by this share of the first candle's range, so the third signal fires a little before an exact touch. 0 needs a precise touch.

settings.label: Direction
settings.html: Which sides the table lists: both, only long entries or only short entries. The markers are not affected.

settings.label: Only Bullish
settings.html: When off, long entries are left out of the table.

settings.label: Only Bearish
settings.html: When off, short entries are left out of the table.

settings.label: Display Rows
settings.html: How many of the most recent third signals the table lists. 0 leaves only the header.

settings.label: Table Position
settings.html: Where the table sits. Tables pin to a corner, so a centre column is drawn on the right and a middle row at the bottom.

settings.label: Table Size
settings.html: Kept for the text size of the table; the table is drawn at the chart's own text size in this version.

settings.label: Style
settings.html: Style of the order block line: solid, dashed or dotted.

settings.label: Width
settings.html: Thickness of the order block line, from 1 to 10.

faq.q: Why can signal 2 never appear on the same candle as signal 1?
faq.html: Signal 2 must be a candle of the opposite colour to the first candle, closing beyond it, and the first candle cannot close beyond its own high or low. It always lands on a later candle.

faq.q: What does the Vertical Offset do?
faq.html: It moves the order block level away from the first candle by a share of that candle's range: above its high for a long, below its low for a short. At 50 the level sits half the candle's range beyond the extreme, so a shallower pullback is enough for signal 3.

faq.q: Why is there only one line on the chart?
faq.html: The line always shows the newest first candle's level. When a new first candle appears, the old line is removed and a new one is drawn from the new candle.

faq.q: Which time zone does the table use?
faq.html: The table writes each signal's time in the chart's own timezone, as hour and minute plus the date on an intraday chart, and the date alone on a daily one.

retracement-to-order-block-with-screener.deviation: The table is drawn at the chart's own text size whatever Table Size says, and a middle row or centre column is drawn in the nearest corner, because a table here has no size setting and pins only to a corner.

smart-money-radar.title: Smart Money Radar
smart-money-radar.summary: Order blocks, fair value gaps, equal highs and lows, prior day, week and month levels, session ranges and BOS or CHoCH labels in one overlay.
smart-money-radar.descriptionHtml:
Smart Money Radar draws several price-structure tools on one chart. Order blocks come from a break of structure: when the close crosses above the last confirmed swing high (a pivot with Pivot Length bars on each side), the study walks back up to 50 bars for the last bearish candle and marks its high-to-low range as a bullish block. A close below the last swing low marks the last bullish candle as a bearish block. A block is removed, or kept faded, the first time a later bar trades into its range, and it is dropped once it is older than the maximum age.

Fair value gaps are three-bar gaps: bullish when the low of the newest bar of the three is above the high of the oldest, bearish in the mirror case. The box is anchored on the middle bar, stops extending once price trades into it, disappears when price crosses it completely, and, with Fade With Age on, grows more transparent as it ages. Equal highs and equal lows compare each new swing point with the five before it; a match within the tolerance, and inside the lookback, draws a dashed liquidity line that is marked as swept when price trades through it and removed five bars later.

The study also plots the previous completed day, week (Monday to Sunday) and month high and low, built from the chart's own bars in UTC, and boxes the Asia (00:00 to 08:00), London (07:00 to 16:00) and New York (12:00 to 21:00) UTC session ranges, keeping the last ten of each with dotted rays at the last five highs and lows. Finally, a longer structure pivot drives the BOS and CHoCH labels: a close through the last structure pivot is a break of structure when it agrees with the current direction, and a change of character when it reverses it.
smart-money-radar.howToReadHtml:
Read the boxes as zones where price may react. A fresh order block or an untouched fair value gap ahead of price marks an area where price moved away quickly, and some traders watch it for a pause or a reversal; once price trades into it, the zone counts as used and is removed or faded. Equal highs and equal lows are two swing points at nearly the same price, often read as a place where stop orders gather, so a swept label shows a level that price has just traded through by more than the tolerance. The day, week and month lines and the session boxes add the prior period and session extremes as reference prices.

BOS labels in one colour show the trend continuing; a CHoCH label shows the first close through the opposite swing and is often read as an early sign of a turn. Every pivot is confirmed only after its right-hand bars have closed, so labels and zones appear a few bars after the swing that created them. None of these marks predicts direction on its own: treat them as a map of recent structure, not as entry signals.

settings.label: Pivot Length (BOS validation)
settings.html: Bars on each side of a swing point used for order blocks and equal levels. Higher values find fewer, larger swings.

settings.label: Max Age (bars)
settings.html: An order block older than this many bars, counted from its candle, is removed.

settings.label: Keep Mitigated Blocks (faded)
settings.html: Keep a block that price has traded into, faded and stopped at that bar, instead of removing it.

settings.label: Bullish OB

settings.label: Bearish OB

settings.label: Border Width

settings.label: Fair Value Gaps

settings.label: Min Size (% of price)
settings.html: Ignore gaps smaller than this percentage of the close. 0 keeps every gap.

settings.label: FVG Max Age (bars)
settings.html: A gap older than this many bars is removed; it also sets how quickly gaps fade.

settings.label: Fade With Age
settings.html: Make each gap more transparent as it gets older, so fresh gaps stand out.

settings.label: Bullish FVG
settings.html: Colour of bullish fair value gaps.

settings.label: Bearish FVG

settings.label: Equal Highs / Equal Lows
settings.html: Draw equal-high and equal-low liquidity lines and mark them when they are swept.

settings.label: Equal Level Tolerance (% of price)
settings.html: How close two swing points must be, as a percentage of price, to count as equal. Also the distance price must pass the level by to sweep it.

settings.label: Lookback (bars)
settings.html: The furthest back, in bars, an earlier swing point may be to pair with a new one.

settings.label: Previous Day H/L
settings.html: Plot the high and low of the previous completed UTC day.

settings.label: Previous Week H/L

settings.label: Previous Month H/L

settings.html: Colour of the equal-high and equal-low lines and their labels.

settings.label: Sessions
settings.html: Draw the session range boxes on intraday charts. Turning it off hides all three sessions.

settings.label: Asia (00:00-08:00 UTC)
settings.html: Draw the Asia session range, 00:00 to 08:00 UTC.

settings.label: London (07:00-16:00 UTC)
settings.html: Draw the London session range, 07:00 to 16:00 UTC.

settings.label: New York (12:00-21:00 UTC)
settings.html: Draw the New York session range, 12:00 to 21:00 UTC.

settings.label: Asia
settings.html: Colour of the Asia session box and rays.

settings.label: London
settings.html: Colour of the London session box and rays.

settings.label: New York
settings.html: Colour of the New York session box and rays.

settings.label: Keep H/L Lines After Session
settings.html: When a session ends, leave dotted rays at its high and low, keeping the last five of each.

settings.label: BOS / CHoCH
settings.html: Draw break of structure and change of character lines and labels.

settings.label: Structure Pivot Length
settings.html: Bars on each side of the structure pivots. Higher values give fewer, more significant breaks.

settings.label: BOS
settings.html: Colour of break of structure lines and labels.

settings.label: CHoCH

settings.label: Watermark
settings.html: Show a small panel with the study's name in a corner of the chart.

settings.label: Watermark Position

settings.label: Watermark Text Size
settings.html: Has no effect in this version: a table cell takes no text size, so the panel always uses the chart's standard table text.

faq.q: Why do order blocks and labels appear a few bars after the swing?
faq.html: Every swing point needs its right-hand bars to close before it is confirmed: five bars for the order block pivots and seven for the structure pivots by default. Nothing is drawn until then, so a swing point is never redrawn at a different bar or price once it is confirmed. Zones and equal levels can still be removed later, when price trades into them or they age out.

faq.q: What is the difference between BOS and CHoCH?
faq.html: Both are a close through the last confirmed structure pivot. It is labelled BOS when the break is in the same direction as the previous break, and CHoCH when it is the first break in the opposite direction.

faq.q: Why did an order block vanish?
faq.html: A block is removed the first time a later bar trades into its range, or when it becomes older than the maximum age. Turn on Keep Mitigated Blocks to keep used blocks on the chart, faded and stopped at the bar that touched them.

faq.q: Which timezone do the sessions and previous day levels use?
faq.html: UTC throughout. The sessions are fixed UTC windows and the day, week and month levels are built from UTC calendar boundaries, whatever timezone the chart axis shows. The session boxes are only drawn on intraday charts.

magnetic-zones-multi-timeframe.title: Magnetic Zones Multi-timeframe
magnetic-zones-multi-timeframe.summary: Projects Fibonacci-spaced support and resistance zones from the previous day, week or month, with optional averages, VWAP and Supertrend.
magnetic-zones-multi-timeframe.descriptionHtml:
Magnetic Zones turns the previous higher timeframe bar into a ladder of price levels for the current one. On the first chart bar of each new day, week or month, the study takes the previous period's high and low, marks their midpoint as the pivot, and places resistance levels above it and support levels below it at 0.236, 0.786, 1.618, 2.618, 4.236 and 6.618 times the previous period's range. These are the six pairs SR1 to SR6.

SR1, SR2, SR4 and SR6 each carry a buffer box around both levels, a band one eighth of the gap to the neighbouring level on either side, so a level reads as a zone rather than a single price; SR3 and SR5 are drawn as lines only. SR1 also gets a wider box spanning from just above R1 to just below S1, the area around the pivot. The previous period's high and low (PDHL) and the pivot are drawn as lines. Three timeframes can be drawn at once, each with its own line style and its own count of past periods to keep. A timeframe code is blank for the chart itself, a number for minutes, or D, W or M; day, week and month periods follow the chart's own calendar.

Four optional overlays share the chart. Two moving averages, exponential (seeded with a simple average) or simple, can run on the chart's bars or on a folded higher timeframe, in which case every chart bar reads the value the previous higher timeframe bar closed with. An anchored VWAP restarts each day, week or month, and a Supertrend ratchets its bands against the previous close and flips direction on the current close.
magnetic-zones-multi-timeframe.howToReadHtml:
Read the zones as a ladder of reference prices for the current period, measured from where the previous period traded. The SR1 box around the pivot covers the middle of the previous range, about 0.3 of its width on each side of the midpoint. SR2 sits beyond the previous high and low, about 0.29 of the previous range outside them, so price at SR2 has already left the last period's range. SR3 to SR6 sit 1.618 to 6.618 previous ranges from the pivot and are reached only when price travels far beyond the previous range. The previous high and low lines show where the last period's range ended.

The levels are fixed for the whole period once its first bar prints, so they never move intraday. They describe the previous period's range, not a forecast, and on a quiet previous period the zones sit close together and are crossed often. The moving averages, the VWAP and the Supertrend add a trend read beside the ladder; none of them changes where the zones are drawn.

settings.html: Draw the Supertrend line, green while it trails below price and red while it sits above.

settings.label: ATR Length
settings.html: Bars in the average true range that sets the Supertrend's distance.

settings.label: Factor
settings.html: How many average true ranges the Supertrend bands sit from the bar's midpoint.

faq.q: Why do the zones not move during the day?
faq.html: Every level is measured from the previous period's high and low, which are final once the new period opens. The study draws them on the period's first bar and only extends them to the right after that.

faq.q: Why are there three boxes around the pivot?
faq.html: With SR1 on, one wide box spans from just above R1 to just below S1, the area around the pivot. The two boxes inside it are the buffers around R1 and S1 themselves, drawn ten transparency points fainter and captioned with the level's price and the timeframe code.

faq.q: Why are SR3 and SR5 drawn without boxes?
faq.html: The study draws buffer boxes for SR1, SR2, SR4 and SR6 only. SR3 and SR5 are plain lines in the colours of their neighbours, so turning them on adds two lines per period and no boxes.

faq.q: How does a higher timeframe moving average avoid looking ahead?
faq.html: The chart's bars are folded into higher timeframe bars, and every chart bar inside a period reads the average as it stood when the previous period closed. The value changes only when a new period opens.

futures-context.title: Futures Context
futures-context.summary: Folds same-time RVOL, realized volatility, session VWAP location, EMA structure and trend quality into one session regime verdict with a confidence score.
futures-context.descriptionHtml:
Futures Context is a session study for intraday index futures. It measures five things on every bar and folds them into one verdict. Participation compares each session bar's volume with the average volume of the same time slot over past sessions, the same-time RVOL, and also compares session-to-date volume with what those baselines expected by now. Volatility divides a rolling realized volatility, the square root of summed squared log returns, by its own exponential average. Location tracks the session VWAP, how far price sits from it in units of its volume-weighted dispersion, its slope in ATRs and how often closes cross it.

Structure comes from a fast, mid and slow exponential average: whether they are stacked, how far apart they are in ATRs and whether price is pulling back between them. Trend quality blends the ADX, directional efficiency (net move over the path travelled), the EMA separation and the VWAP slope. A direction score adds up the EMA stack, the VWAP side and slope, the DI lines, efficiency and the side of the session open.

From these the study builds four scores between 0 and 1: trend quality, expansion, compression and balance. The regime is then chosen in order: Outside RTH, Compression, Bull or Bear Expansion, Bull or Bear Trend, Balanced Rotation, Volatility Expansion, and Transition when nothing qualifies. The confidence is how strongly the measures behind the chosen verdict agree. The pane plots the bar RVOL, the cumulative RVOL, the realized volatility ratio and, if switched on, the developing range ratio, all around a dashed baseline at 1.
futures-context.howToReadHtml:
Read every plotted line against the dashed line at 1, which means normal for this time of day or this instrument. A bar RVOL column well above 1 is a bar trading far more than that slot usually does; a cumulative RVOL above 1 means the whole session is busier than usual. A realized volatility ratio above 1 means the market is moving more than its recent norm. The dashboard on the newest bar gives the regime, its confidence, the bias as a percentage from -100 to +100, and each measure behind them.

The same-time baselines need a minute-based intraday chart no longer than the maximum supported timeframe, a correct session and time zone, and enough past sessions; until then the RVOL plots are empty and participation reads Warming Up. On an hourly chart at the default settings only the volatility ratio is drawn. The relative strength input of the regime is always zero, because the study reads one instrument. The verdict describes conditions so far; it does not forecast the next bar.

settings.label: Enable indicator
settings.html: Turns the plots and the dashboard on or off. The calculation keeps running either way, so the alerts still work when it is off.

settings.label: Analysis time zone
settings.html: The IANA time zone the session hours, the session date and the session phases are read in, such as America/New_York. A name the host does not know stops the study, so spell it exactly.

settings.label: Classify outside RTH
settings.html: When off, every bar outside the regular session is reported as Outside RTH. When on, those bars get a full regime verdict from the technical measures, with no participation input.

settings.label: RTH session
settings.html: The regular session as HHMM-HHMM:days, with days numbered 1 for Sunday through 7 for Saturday. A bar is in the session when its open time falls inside the window. An end before the start crosses midnight, an equal start and end such as 0000-0000 is a full 24 hours, and text that does not follow this form puts no bar in the session.

settings.label: RTH open hour
settings.html: The hour of the session open, in the analysis time zone. Same-time slots are counted in chart intervals from this open.

settings.label: RTH open minute
settings.html: The minute of the session open. Together with the open hour it fixes slot 0 of every session.

settings.label: Historical sessions
settings.html: How many past sessions each same-time slot remembers. Older sessions drop out of the baseline as new ones arrive.

settings.label: Minimum samples before display
settings.html: How many past sessions a slot needs before its RVOL and range ratio are shown and scored. Until then participation reads Warming Up.

settings.label: Maximum supported chart timeframe
settings.html: The largest chart interval, in minutes, on which the same-time baselines run. On a longer interval the RVOL and range plots stay empty.

settings.label: Elevated bar RVOL
settings.html: Bar RVOL at or above this reads as Elevated participation and earns the full bar participation score.

settings.label: Extreme bar RVOL
settings.html: Bar RVOL at or above this reads as Extreme participation. It also sets where the column shading reaches full strength.

settings.label: Elevated cumulative RVOL
settings.html: Session-to-date RVOL at or above this reads as Elevated participation and earns the full cumulative participation score.

settings.label: Quiet RVOL
settings.html: Participation is Quiet when both the bar RVOL and the cumulative RVOL are at or below this level. It also sets where the shading of columns below 1 reaches full strength.

settings.label: Rolling return window
settings.html: The number of bars of squared log returns summed into the rolling realized volatility.

settings.label: Volatility baseline length
settings.html: The length of the exponential average of realized volatility that the volatility ratio divides by.

settings.label: Volatility z-score length
settings.html: The window of the mean and standard deviation behind the realized volatility z-score shown in the dashboard.

settings.label: Expansion ratio
settings.html: A volatility ratio at or above this reads as Expanding, and it is where the volatility expansion score reaches 1.

settings.label: Contraction ratio
settings.html: A volatility ratio at or below this reads as Contracting in the dashboard.

settings.label: VWAP source
settings.html: The price each bar contributes to the session VWAP and to its volume-weighted dispersion.

settings.label: VWAP slope lookback
settings.html: How many bars back the VWAP slope is measured. The slope is only taken once the session has run at least this many same-time slots, so on a chart longer than the maximum supported timeframe it is never taken and scores as zero.

settings.label: VWAP crossing lookback
settings.html: The number of bars over which closes crossing the VWAP are counted for the rotation test.

settings.label: Strong VWAP slope (ATR)
settings.html: A VWAP slope of this many ATRs or more earns the full slope score in trend quality.

settings.label: Rotation distance (sigma)
settings.html: Price counts as rotating only while its VWAP z-score is within this many dispersions of the VWAP.

settings.label: Crosses indicating rotation
settings.html: How many VWAP crossings in the lookback mark the session as rotating. It also scales the crossing part of the balance score.

settings.label: EMA source
settings.html: The price the three exponential averages are computed on.

settings.label: Fast EMA
settings.html: Length of the fast exponential average, the first line of the stack and the one whose slope is measured.

settings.label: Mid EMA
settings.html: Length of the middle exponential average, also the line price is compared with when the stack is tangled.

settings.label: Slow EMA
settings.html: Length of the slow exponential average, the last line of the stack.

settings.label: Slope lookback
settings.html: How many bars back the fast average's slope is measured, in ATR units.

settings.label: Compression spread (ATR)
settings.html: An EMA spread at or below this many ATRs reads as Compressed. The EMA part of the compression score is full at no spread and falls to zero at this level.

settings.label: Expansion spread (ATR)
settings.html: An EMA spread at or above this many ATRs counts as expanded, and it is where the separation score reaches 1.

settings.label: ATR length
settings.html: The average true range length used to put EMA spreads and slopes and the VWAP slope in ATR units.

settings.label: DI length
settings.html: Smoothing length of the true range and directional movement behind the two DI lines.

settings.label: ADX smoothing
settings.html: Smoothing length applied to the DI spread to give the ADX.

settings.label: Weak ADX
settings.html: ADX at or below this reads as a Weak trend. It is the start of the ADX score and the end of the ADX compression score.

settings.label: Strong ADX
settings.html: ADX at or above this reads as a Strong trend and earns the full ADX score.

settings.label: Directional efficiency length
settings.html: The window over which net movement is divided by the total path travelled.

settings.label: Weak efficiency
settings.html: Efficiency at or below this adds nothing to trend quality. It is also where the efficiency part of the compression score reaches zero, falling from its full value at zero efficiency.

settings.label: Strong efficiency
settings.html: Efficiency at or above this earns the full efficiency score and removes the low efficiency part of balance.

settings.label: Directional threshold
settings.html: The absolute direction score a bar needs before a trend or an expansion verdict can take a side.

settings.label: Trend-quality threshold
settings.html: Trend quality at or above this, with a directional bias, gives a Bull Trend or Bear Trend verdict.

settings.label: Expansion threshold
settings.html: An expansion score at or above this gives an expansion verdict, directional when the bias is strong enough.

settings.label: Compression threshold
settings.html: A compression score at or above this, without expansion, gives the Compression verdict.

settings.label: Balance threshold
settings.html: A balance score at or above this gives the Balanced Rotation verdict when no trend or expansion applies.

settings.label: Range expansion ratio
settings.html: A developing range ratio at or above this reads as Expanded and earns the full range expansion score.

settings.label: Range compression ratio
settings.html: A developing range ratio at or below this reads as Compressed in the dashboard. The range part of the compression score falls from full at a ratio of 0.45 to zero at this level.

settings.label: Show bar RVOL histogram
settings.html: Draws the same-time bar RVOL as columns, shaded by how far it sits from the baseline.

settings.label: Show cumulative RVOL
settings.html: Draws session-to-date volume against the volume the baselines expected by this slot.

settings.label: Show realized-volatility ratio
settings.html: Draws rolling realized volatility over its own exponential baseline.

settings.label: Show developing-range ratio
settings.html: Draws the session's high to low range so far over the average range past sessions had reached by the same slot.

settings.label: Visual plot cap
settings.html: Plotted values above this are drawn at the cap, so one spike does not flatten the pane. The dashboard and alerts use the uncapped values.

settings.label: Show context dashboard
settings.html: Shows the table with the regime, its confidence and every measure behind it for the newest bar.

settings.label: RVOL alert threshold
settings.html: The same-time RVOL alert fires on a session bar whose RVOL reaches this level after being below it.

settings.label: Volatility alert threshold
settings.html: The volatility alert fires on the bar the realized volatility ratio reaches this level after being below it.

faq.q: Why are the RVOL plots empty on my chart?
faq.html: Same-time RVOL runs only on an intraday chart whose interval is at most the maximum supported timeframe, 30 minutes by default, and only on bars inside the RTH session. Each time slot also needs the minimum number of past sessions before it is shown. On an hourly chart, raise the maximum supported timeframe to 60 to turn it on.

faq.q: How are the session days numbered?
faq.html: In the RTH session setting the days run 1 for Sunday through 7 for Saturday, so 23456 is Monday to Friday. The bars are tested in the analysis time zone, and a bar belongs to the session when its open time is inside the window. For a window that crosses midnight, such as 1800-1700, the hours after midnight count as the day the window opened on. For a market that trades all day, write 0000-0000.

faq.q: What does the confidence number mean?
faq.html: It is the agreement of the measures behind the chosen regime, as a percentage. For a trend it averages trend quality, the strength of the bias and the lack of balance; for compression or balance it is that score itself. Outside RTH it is 100, and for Transition it is held between 35 and 72.

faq.q: Does the study use a second instrument for relative strength?
faq.html: No. The regime engine has a slot for relative strength against another instrument, but this study reads only the chart's own bars, so that part of the direction score is always zero and the dashboard says so.

futures-context.deviation: The bar RVOL columns rise from the pane's axis rather than from the baseline of 1, because a plot has no base setting in this OpenScript version; and a time zone name that is not recognised stops the study instead of falling back to America/New_York, because a zone name cannot be checked before it is used.

related.summary: Projects Fibonacci-spaced support and resistance zones from the previous day, week or month, with optional averages, VWAP and Supertrend.

futures-levels.title: Futures Levels
futures-levels.summary: A session level map for intraday futures: opening range, initial balance, overnight range, anchored VWAP bands, prior day and week, confluence zones and level states.
futures-levels.descriptionHtml:
Futures Levels draws the reference prices an intraday futures trader watches, all read in one session time zone. It tracks three sessions you write as clock windows: the full session, the overnight session and the regular trading hours (RTH). From them it builds the opening range and the initial balance, the high and low of the first minutes after the regular open; the overnight high and low; the session opens; and the previous day and previous week highs and lows, where a trading day that starts in the evening counts toward the next calendar day, as a futures daily bar does.

An anchored VWAP restarts at the regular open, the full session open or the start of each week, and sums price times volume from there. Its bands sit a chosen number of deviations away, where the deviation is either volume weighted or a plain per-bar measure. Optional Fibonacci levels split a chosen range at three retracement ratios and project it beyond each end at three more.

Two engines work over these levels. The acceptance and rejection engine watches seventeen of them on every bar: a run of closes beyond a level by a buffer is an acceptance, and a bar that wicks into a level from one side and closes back away by the buffer, with a wick of at least a minimum size, is a rejection. The confluence engine takes the levels visible on the newest bar, sorts them by price, groups those within a tolerance of the group's weighted centre, and draws the highest-scoring groups as zones. Vertical markers at 08:30, 09:30, 11:00 and 16:00 session time and a compact table complete the picture.
futures-levels.howToReadHtml:
Read the lines as a map of where the session has already found buyers and sellers. Price holding beyond the opening range or initial balance after its window closes is often read as a trend day, and a return inside the range as rotation. The VWAP and its bands show where the session's volume has traded on average, and a confluence zone, especially one listing several names, marks a price where several references meet, which is where traders tend to watch for a reaction.

The state labels and alerts say what price did at a level, not what it will do next: an acceptance needs the set number of closes beyond it, so it always arrives after the move has started. The levels depend on the session windows matching the instrument, and the opening range needs bars finer than its window: on an hourly chart a 15-minute range never forms, which is why the table asks for 30-minute or finer bars.

settings.label: Enable indicator
settings.html: Turns the whole study on or off. Off, it draws no lines, labels, boxes, shading or table.

settings.label: Session time zone
settings.html: The IANA time zone every session, opening time and time marker is read in, such as America/New_York or Asia/Kolkata. A blank field uses America/New_York; a name the chart does not recognise stops the study with a message.

settings.label: Show prices in horizontal labels
settings.html: Adds the level's price after its name in each horizontal label on the newest bar.

settings.label: Show horizontal line labels
settings.html: Draws a name label beside each visible level on the newest bar.

settings.label: Horizontal-label wording
settings.html: Compact writes short tags such as ORH and PDH; Descriptive writes them out in full, such as OPENING RANGE HIGH.

settings.label: Horizontal-label height (ticks)
settings.html: How many ticks above its level each horizontal label sits, so the text clears the line.

settings.label: Full futures session
settings.html: The full trading session as HHMM-HHMM with an optional day list after a colon, 1 for Sunday through 7 for Saturday. It sets the session open and the trading day the previous-day high and low are folded over. A spec that does not follow the form falls back to the default.

settings.label: Overnight session
settings.html: The overnight window, written the same way. Its high and low become the overnight levels once it ends.

settings.label: RTH session
settings.html: The regular trading hours window, written the same way. The opening range, the initial balance and the default VWAP anchor all fall inside it.

settings.label: RTH open (hour)
settings.html: The hour, in the session time zone, that the opening range and initial balance windows start from.

settings.label: RTH open (minute)
settings.html: The minute past that hour the opening range and initial balance windows start from.

settings.label: Shade sessions
settings.html: Shades the background: strongest while the opening range forms, lighter for the rest of the regular session, faintest overnight.

settings.label: Show futures / RTH opens
settings.html: Draws the full session open and the regular session open as lines, and tracks both in the state engine and the clusters.

settings.label: Show overnight high / low
settings.html: Draws the overnight high and low during the overnight and regular sessions, and tracks them once the overnight window has closed.

settings.label: Show overnight midpoint
settings.html: Adds the midpoint between the overnight high and low.

settings.label: Show Opening Range
settings.html: Draws the opening range high and low during the regular session.

settings.label: Opening Range duration
settings.html: How long the opening range window runs from the regular open. A chart bar counts when any part of it overlaps the window.

settings.label: Show while developing
settings.html: Shows the opening range while it is still forming. Off, the lines appear only once the window has closed.

settings.label: Show midpoint
settings.html: Adds the opening range midpoint line and its label.

settings.label: Fill range
settings.html: Shades a box over the latest opening range, from its first bar to the newest bar or the end of the regular session.

settings.label: Show vertical time markers
settings.html: Draws vertical lines at 08:30, 09:30, 11:00 and 16:00 in the session time zone on an intraday chart.

settings.label: Show time-marker labels
settings.html: Adds a caption above each vertical time marker.

settings.label: Marker-label layout
settings.html: Stacked puts each word of a caption on its own line; Single line keeps it on one.

settings.label: Marker-label top padding (ATR)
settings.html: How far above the day's high a caption sits, in multiples of the 14-bar ATR. Raise it if captions overlap candles.

settings.label: Maximum marker events
settings.html: How many of the most recent time markers are kept; older ones are removed.

settings.label: Marker transparency
settings.html: How faint the vertical marker lines are, from 65 to 96 percent transparent.

settings.label: Show Initial Balance
settings.html: Draws the initial balance high and low during the regular session.

settings.label: Initial Balance duration (minutes)
settings.html: How many minutes the initial balance window runs from the regular open.

settings.label: Show Initial Balance while developing
settings.html: Shows the initial balance while it is still forming. Off, the lines appear once the window has closed.

settings.label: Show Initial Balance midpoint
settings.html: Adds the initial balance midpoint line and its label.

settings.label: Fill Initial Balance range
settings.html: Shades a box over the latest initial balance, from its first bar to the newest bar or the end of the regular session.

settings.label: Show VWAP
settings.html: Draws the anchored VWAP and its bands.

settings.label: vwapAnchor
settings.html: Where the VWAP restarts: the regular session open, the full session open, or the start of each week. With RTH or the full session, the line is drawn only inside that session unless carried.

settings.label: Source
settings.html: The price each bar contributes to the VWAP, the typical price by default.

settings.label: Deviation method
settings.html: Volume-weighted measures the band width from volume-weighted squared distance; Unweighted gives every bar in the anchor the same weight.

settings.label: Carry VWAP outside anchor session
settings.html: Keeps drawing the VWAP and bands after the anchor session ends, until the next one starts.

settings.label: Band 1
settings.html: Draws the first pair of deviation bands, and lets the state engine track them.

settings.label: Band 1 multiplier
settings.html: How many deviations the first band pair sits from the VWAP.

settings.label: Band 2
settings.html: Draws the second pair of deviation bands.

settings.label: Band 2 multiplier
settings.html: How many deviations the second band pair sits from the VWAP.

settings.label: Band 3
settings.html: Draws the third pair of deviation bands.

settings.label: Band 3 multiplier
settings.html: How many deviations the third band pair sits from the VWAP.

settings.label: Show previous day high / low
settings.html: Draws the previous trading day's high and low.

settings.label: Previous-day source
settings.html: Exchange daily bar folds every bar of the full session into the trading day; Custom RTH session uses only the regular session's high and low.

settings.label: Show previous week high / low
settings.html: Draws the previous week's high and low, with weeks built from trading days starting on Monday.

settings.label: Show Fibonacci levels
settings.html: Draws Fibonacci retracements and range projections off the chosen anchor range.

settings.label: Anchor range
settings.html: The range the Fibonacci levels are measured from: the finished opening range or initial balance, the finished overnight range, the previous day or the previous week.

settings.label: Show internal retracements
settings.html: Draws the three levels inside the anchor range.

settings.label: Show symmetric range projections
settings.html: Draws the three projections above the range high and the three below the range low.

settings.label: Retracement 1
settings.html: The first retracement, as a fraction of the range measured up from its low.

settings.label: Retracement 2
settings.html: The second retracement, as a fraction of the range measured up from its low.

settings.label: Retracement 3
settings.html: The third retracement, as a fraction of the range measured up from its low.

settings.label: Projection 1
settings.html: The first projection, as a fraction of the range added above the high and subtracted below the low. 0.272 gives the 1.272 and -0.272 levels.

settings.label: Projection 2
settings.html: The second projection, as a fraction of the range beyond each end.

settings.label: Projection 3
settings.html: The third projection, as a fraction of the range beyond each end.

settings.label: Show current confluence clusters
settings.html: Groups the levels visible on the newest bar into confluence zones and draws the strongest as boxes with a label.

settings.label: Include day / week references
settings.html: Lets the previous day and week highs and lows join the clusters.

settings.label: Include OR / IB / overnight
settings.html: Lets the opening range, initial balance, overnight levels and session opens join the clusters.

settings.label: Include VWAP / bands
settings.html: Lets the VWAP and its bands join the clusters.

settings.label: Include visible Fib levels
settings.html: Lets the visible Fibonacci levels join the clusters.

settings.label: Tolerance mode
settings.html: Whether the distance that groups levels is set in ticks or as a fraction of the ATR.

settings.label: Tolerance (ticks)
settings.html: The grouping distance in ticks when the mode is Ticks.

settings.label: ATR length
settings.html: The ATR length used when the grouping distance is set by ATR.

settings.label: ATR tolerance factor
settings.html: The grouping distance as a fraction of the ATR when the mode is ATR.

settings.label: Minimum contributors
settings.html: How many levels a group needs before it counts as a confluence zone.

settings.label: Maximum displayed clusters
settings.html: How many of the highest-scoring zones are drawn.

settings.label: Zone width left (bars)
settings.html: How many bars to the left of the newest bar each zone box starts.

settings.label: Zone padding (ticks)
settings.html: Ticks added above and below each zone so a tight group still shows as a box.

settings.label: Show contributor names
settings.html: Lists the levels that make up each zone in its label, up to six names.

settings.label: Zone transparency
settings.html: How transparent each zone's fill is, from 60 to 100 percent.

settings.label: Enable acceptance / rejection engine
settings.html: Runs the acceptance and rejection test against the tracked levels on every bar. Off, no states, labels or alerts are produced.

settings.label: Recolor levels by latest state
settings.html: Turns a level line green while its latest state is bullish and red while it is bearish.

settings.label: Touch tolerance mode
settings.html: Whether the touch distance for a rejection is set in ticks or as a fraction of the state ATR.

settings.label: Touch tolerance (ticks)
settings.html: How close, in ticks, a wick must come to a level to count as a touch when the mode is Ticks.

settings.label: State ATR length
settings.html: The ATR length used for touch distances in ATR mode, for the minimum wick and to rank events.

settings.label: Touch tolerance (ATR)
settings.html: The touch distance as a fraction of the state ATR when the mode is ATR.

settings.label: Acceptance buffer (ticks)
settings.html: How many ticks beyond a level a close must be to count as being above or below it.

settings.label: Closes required for acceptance
settings.html: How many closes in a row beyond a level, by the buffer, make an acceptance.

settings.label: Minimum rejection wick (ATR)
settings.html: The smallest rejection wick, in multiples of the state ATR.

settings.label: Show acceptance / rejection labels
settings.html: Draws a label on each bar that produced an acceptance or rejection, at the level that won that bar.

settings.label: Maximum state labels
settings.html: How many of the most recent state labels are kept.

settings.label: Per-level rejection cooldown (bars)
settings.html: How many bars must pass after an event on a level before that level can report another rejection. Acceptances are not held back.

settings.label: Show compact HUD
settings.html: Shows the table with the current session, the opening range and initial balance sizes, the VWAP and the latest state event.

faq.q: Why do I see no opening range on an hourly chart?
faq.html: The opening range is built from the bars that overlap a window of 1 to 30 minutes after the regular open. With 09:30 as the open and hourly bars that start on the hour, no bar inside the regular session overlaps the first 15 or 30 minutes, so the range never forms. Use 15-minute bars or finer.

faq.q: Which time zone are the sessions read in?
faq.html: Every session, the regular open and the time markers are read in the Session time zone setting, not in the chart's own zone. The defaults are written in New York time, so on another market change the zone and the three session windows together.

faq.q: How is the previous day high different from a calendar day high?
faq.html: With Exchange daily bar, the day is the trading day of the full session, so when the session opens in the evening, everything from that open onwards belongs to the next day. With Custom RTH session, only the regular session's bars count.

faq.q: What decides which level gets the label when several react on one bar?
faq.html: Each event is scored by the level's weight, doubled for an acceptance, divided by one plus the distance from the close to the level in ATR units. The highest score wins the bar, and that event is the one labelled, alerted and shown in the table.

futures-levels.deviation: The midpoint, Fibonacci and previous day and week lines are drawn solid rather than dotted or dashed, because a plot has no dotted or dashed style; the VWAP anchor menu is titled vwapAnchor in the settings dialog, because its setting is filed under its title and vwapAnchor is a built-in name; the acceptance and rejection labels are plain plates at the level price rather than pointed tags, because a drawn label has no pointer shape; and a time zone name that is not recognised stops the study instead of falling back to America/New_York, because a zone name cannot be checked before it is used.
