futures-profile.title: Futures Profile
futures-profile.summary: A regular-session TPO profile with a developing POC and value area, the initial balance and its extensions, and the previous session's levels.
futures-profile.descriptionHtml:
Futures Profile builds a time-price-opportunity (TPO) profile of each regular trading session. The session is cut into fixed blocks of time (30 minutes by default) and the price axis into rows a fixed number of ticks tall. Every block marks each row its high-low range touched, so a row's count is the number of blocks that traded there. The busiest row is the point of control (POC); among equally busy rows the one nearest the middle of the profile wins. The value area grows from the POC one row at a time toward the busier neighbour until it holds the chosen share of all marks (70% by default), and its top and bottom are the VAH and VAL.

The profile develops through the session: the block still forming counts toward it, so the POC, VAH, VAL and the profile midpoint move bar by bar. In Auto mode the row height is the previous session's range divided by the target row count, rounded up to whole ticks; a block that would cover more rows than the per-block limit is left out of the profile. The initial balance is the high and low of the first blocks of the session (two by default), and its extensions sit a chosen multiple of its range beyond each side.

When a session ends, its finished profile becomes the previous profile. Its POC, VAH and VAL are carried into the next session and coloured by how price treats them. The POC turns green after the chosen number of consecutive closes above it, or after a test that closes at or above it, and red for the same below. The VAH turns green when closes hold above it and red when a test closes back below it; the VAL turns red when closes hold below it and green when a test closes back above it. A VAH or VAL that has not been judged yet in the session is amber on a bar that tests it. These judgements start afresh at each session open. A previous extreme with more than one mark on its outermost row is drawn as a poor high or poor low, and runs of single-mark rows are shaded as single-print zones. An optional estimated volume profile spreads each bar's volume evenly across the rows it touched. On the newest bar the study draws both profiles as boxes and fills a dashboard that classifies the session's shape, auction state and position against the previous value area.
futures-profile.howToReadHtml:
Read the developing value area as the price range the session has accepted so far, and the POC as its fairest price. The dashboard puts the levels into words. When the value area sits higher than the previous one, the POC has moved up by more than half a row and price trades above the initial balance or the developing VAH, it reads Initiative Buying (Initiative Selling is the mirror case). A session that opens above the previous value area and trades back inside it reads Responsive Selling, and, unless the POC has moved up, a Failed Upward Auction; the mirror case below reads Responsive Buying and a Failed Downward Auction. The initial balance and its extensions frame how far the session has ranged from its opening hour. Poor highs and lows and single-print zones mark places the previous session left without a clean rejection or traded only once; the study tints them when price comes back to them, but whether it does is not something the study predicts.

The profile is only as good as its block clock. It is meant for intraday charts at or below the TPO block size; on a coarser chart, or one longer than the maximum chart timeframe setting, the dashboard footer shows a timeframe warning. If a session's bars span more rows than the per-block limit, those blocks are left out and the profile can be empty, so raise the ticks per row or switch to Manual row sizing. The volume profile is an estimate from bar volume, not traded volume at each price.

settings.label: Enable indicator
settings.html: Turns the whole study on or off: levels, profiles, dashboard and alerts.

settings.label: Analysis time zone
settings.html: The IANA time zone, such as America/New_York or Asia/Kolkata, that the session window and the block clock are read in. Blank means America/New_York. A name the host does not know, or an abbreviation such as IST, stops the study with an error rather than falling back, so write the full area and location.

settings.label: RTH session
settings.html: The regular session as HHMM-HHMM, optionally followed by a colon and the trading days, where 1 is Sunday and 7 is Saturday. A window that does not read falls back to 0930-1600 Monday to Friday.

settings.label: RTH open hour
settings.html: The hour the block clock starts from. Blocks are counted from this time, so it should match the session start.

settings.label: Minute
settings.html: The minute of the hour the block clock starts from.

settings.label: TPO block size
settings.html: The length of one TPO block. Shorter blocks give more marks per session and a finer profile.

settings.label: Initial Balance blocks
settings.html: How many blocks from the session start make up the initial balance. Two 30-minute blocks give the usual first hour.

settings.label: Maximum chart timeframe
settings.html: The longest chart interval, in minutes, the dashboard accepts before it shows a timeframe warning.

settings.label: Row-size mode
settings.html: Auto sizes rows from the previous session's range and the target row count; Manual uses a fixed number of ticks per row.

settings.label: Manual ticks per row
settings.html: The row height in ticks when the row-size mode is Manual.

settings.label: Automatic target rows
settings.html: In Auto mode, the number of rows the previous session's range is divided into. More rows means shorter rows.

settings.label: Minimum automatic ticks
settings.html: The smallest row height, in ticks, Auto mode may choose.

settings.label: Maximum rendered rows
settings.html: The most boxes one drawn profile may use. Larger profiles are grouped into bands of rows for drawing; the statistics still use every row.

settings.label: Maximum rows per TPO block
settings.html: A block or bar that spans more rows than this is left out of the profile and raises the row-density warning.

settings.label: Value area percentage
settings.html: The share of all TPO marks the value area must hold. Higher values widen the VAH to VAL range.

settings.label: Show current profile
settings.html: Draw the developing session's profile as boxes from its first bar.

settings.label: Show previous profile
settings.html: Draw the previous completed session's profile as boxes from its first bar.

settings.label: Maximum TPO width (bars)
settings.html: How many bars wide the busiest row of a drawn profile is; other rows are scaled to it.

settings.label: Show TPO count on rows
settings.html: Write each drawn row band's TPO count beside the current profile.

settings.label: Show Current / Previous labels
settings.html: Label the drawn profiles CURRENT TPO, PREVIOUS TPO and EST. VOLUME above their tops.

settings.label: Highlight value-area rows
settings.html: Tint the rows inside the value area differently from the rows outside it in the drawn profiles.

settings.label: Show profile midpoint
settings.html: Plot the midpoint of the developing profile's high and low.

settings.label: Profile transparency
settings.html: How transparent the current profile's boxes are, from 0 (solid) to 90.

settings.label: Previous profile transparency
settings.html: How transparent the previous profile's boxes are, from 0 (solid) to 95.

settings.label: Show current POC / VAH / VAL
settings.html: Plot the developing POC, VAH and VAL.

settings.label: Show previous POC / VAH / VAL
settings.html: Carry the previous session's POC, VAH and VAL through the current session, coloured by acceptance or rejection.

settings.label: Show Initial Balance
settings.html: Plot the initial balance high and low.

settings.label: Show IB range extensions
settings.html: Plot the two extensions above and below the initial balance.

settings.label: First IB extension
settings.html: The first extension's distance beyond the initial balance, as a multiple of its range.

settings.label: Second IB extension
settings.html: The second extension's distance beyond the initial balance, as a multiple of its range.

settings.label: Show session open / close
settings.html: Plot the session's opening price and its latest close, which holds at the final close after the session ends.

settings.label: Closes for prior-value acceptance
settings.html: How many consecutive closes beyond a previous level count as acceptance there.

settings.label: Show previous single-print zones
settings.html: Shade the previous profile's single-print zones during the session, tinted once they are touched or filled.

settings.label: Show previous poor high / low
settings.html: Plot the previous session's high or low when its outermost row has more than one mark.

settings.label: Maximum single-print zones
settings.html: The most single-print zones drawn, lowest first.

settings.label: Show estimated volume profile
settings.html: Build and draw a volume profile that spreads each bar's volume evenly across the rows it touched.

settings.label: Maximum volume width (bars)
settings.html: How many bars wide the heaviest band of the drawn volume profile is.

settings.label: Show estimated VPOC / VAH / VAL
settings.html: Plot the estimated volume profile's POC and value area when the volume profile is on.

settings.label: Estimated volume value area
settings.html: The share of estimated volume the volume value area must hold.

settings.label: Double-distribution secondary peak
settings.html: How busy a second peak must be, as a fraction of the POC's count, to count toward a double distribution.

settings.label: Double-distribution valley ratio
settings.html: How thin the valley between the two peaks must be, as a fraction of the smaller peak, for a double distribution.

settings.label: Minimum peak separation (rows)
settings.html: How many rows a second peak must sit from the POC to count as a separate peak.

settings.label: P / b shape skew threshold
settings.html: The profile skew beyond which the shape reads as P-shaped or b-shaped rather than balanced.

settings.label: Trend-profile range / IB
settings.html: How many times the initial balance range the profile must span before it can read as a trend profile.

settings.label: Strong POC migration (rows)
settings.html: How many rows the POC must move from the previous POC to read as strongly higher or lower.

settings.label: Show Profile dashboard
settings.html: Show the dashboard with the auction, shape, value, structure, open and location readings.

settings.label: Layout with Futures Levels
settings.html: Pin the dashboard to the top right corner. Turn it off to place it with the standalone position setting.

settings.label: Standalone dashboard position
settings.html: The corner the dashboard uses when the stacked layout is off. The middle positions use the top corner on the same side.

settings.label: Dashboard text size
settings.html: Has no effect here: the dashboard uses the chart's table text size.

settings.label: Dashboard column width (%)
settings.html: Has no effect here: the dashboard sizes its columns to their text.

settings.label: Header height (%)
settings.html: Has no effect here: the dashboard sizes its rows to their text.

settings.label: Card row height (%)
settings.html: Has no effect here: the dashboard sizes its rows to their text.

settings.label: Footer height (%)
settings.html: Has no effect here: the dashboard sizes its rows to their text.

settings.label: Alert on previous POC / VAH / VAL
settings.html: Raise an alert on the bar price first tests the previous POC, VAH or VAL.

settings.label: Alert on previous single prints
settings.html: Raise an alert on the bar price first enters a previous single-print zone.

settings.label: Alert on poor high / low repair
settings.html: Raise an alert on the bar price first trades beyond a previous poor high or poor low.

settings.label: Alert on auction-state changes
settings.html: Raise an alert when the auction reading changes during the session.

faq.q: Why are the profile levels missing on my chart?
faq.html: Every block that spans more rows than the per-block limit is left out of the profile. In Auto mode the very first session has no previous range to size rows from and falls back to a few ticks per row, which on a volatile instrument makes every block too tall. That session then leaves no profile behind, so the next one has no range to size from either, and the profile stays empty session after session. Switch to Manual with more ticks per row, or raise the per-block limit, and the profile fills in.

faq.q: Which chart interval should I use?
faq.html: An intraday interval no longer than the TPO block, such as 1, 5 or 15 minutes for 30-minute blocks. On a coarser chart a single bar covers more than one block but is counted in only one, so the profile has fewer marks than the session had blocks, and the dashboard footer shows a timeframe warning.

faq.q: How is the value area built?
faq.html: It starts at the POC row and adds one row at a time, choosing the busier of the row just above and the row just below (the one above on a tie), until it holds the chosen share of all TPO marks.

faq.q: What makes a high or low poor?
faq.html: A profile extreme is poor when its outermost row has more than one mark, which means the session traded there in more than one block without a sharp rejection. The study carries the previous session's poor extremes forward and draws them in grey on the bars where price trades beyond them.

futures-setups-research.title: Futures Setups Research
futures-setups-research.summary: Scores Fair Value Gaps and Order Blocks from the chart and five higher timeframes on a 1-minute futures chart and draws the best qualifying touch as a trade with a stop and 1R to 2R objectives.
futures-setups-research.descriptionHtml:
Futures Setups Research is a setup engine for 1-minute index futures charts. It folds the chart's own bars into 5, 15, 30, 60 and 240 minute buckets that start at the futures session open, and on every bucket and on the chart itself it looks for Fair Value Gaps (a gap between the high of one candle and the low of the candle two later) and Order Blocks (the last opposite candle before a displacement candle that breaks recent structure). Zones that are too narrow or too wide against their own ATR are ignored. When price closes through a zone it is invalidated, and a gap flips into an Inversion FVG and an order block into a Breaker Block of the opposite direction, each with a shorter life.

Every active zone is scored out of 100 on every bar: up to 30 for its timeframe, kind and width, up to 25 for overlapping zones of the same direction, up to 20 for a recent break of structure or displacement, up to 15 for nearby liquidity (repeated swing pools, swept levels, the previous day and week, the overnight range and the opening range), up to 10 for market context (VWAP rejection, a weighted regime blended from all five buckets and the chart, z-score and RSI turns, relative volume at the same time of day) and up to 5 for power-of-three and opening range behaviour. A divergence against a second instrument is not available to a single-chart study, so that last category tops out at 4.

When a zone is touched inside the signal window and passes every gate (score, categories, structure, displacement, touch count, cooldown, one trade per leg, a valid stop and enough room to the nearest objective), the best one becomes a trade: entry at the close, stop just beyond the zone, and objectives at 1R, 1.5R and 2R, each drawn as a band. The trade ends at the stop, at 2R or at the time limit.
futures-setups-research.howToReadHtml:
Read the panel first. Each cell gives a timeframe's regime from STRONG BEAR to STRONG BULL with its score, and ENGINE says READY only on a 1-minute chart (or a 2 to 5 minute chart with that option on) of a supported or allowed instrument; elsewhere the panel is all the study computes. On a ready chart the boxes are the active zones, labelled with their timeframe and kind, and the dashed lines are liquidity pools with at least the minimum number of touches (three by default).

A BUY or SELL label marks a trade entry with its score, and the bands show the risk to the stop and the reward out to 2R. The outcome label (STOP -1R, WIN +2R or a TIME exit) shows how it ended. These are research marks, not instructions: a mark on the newest bar can still change until that bar closes, the score rewards confluence, it does not measure the chance of a win, and when the stop and a target both fall inside one bar the stop is counted first.

settings.label: Enable indicator
settings.html: Turn zone registration on or off. Switched off, no zone is registered, so no zone is drawn and no trade is taken; the liquidity-pool lines and the regime panel still show.

settings.label: Allow symbols other than NQ/ES
settings.html: Let the engine run on an instrument whose ticker does not start with NQ, MNQ, ES or MES. A chart that names no instrument is always allowed.

settings.label: Allow chart timeframes above 1 minute
settings.html: Let the engine run on 2 to 5 minute charts as well as the 1-minute chart. Above 5 minutes the engine stays off and only the regime panel is computed.

settings.label: Session timezone
settings.html: The timezone every session window, the 09:30 opening range and the 17:00 session close are read in. Use a full area and location name such as America/New_York; a name the chart does not know stops the study with an error.

settings.label: Futures session
settings.html: The full futures session, written HHMM-HHMM with optional day digits where 1 is Sunday. It sets where the trading day rolls and when the session VWAP restarts.

settings.label: Overnight session
settings.html: The window whose high and low form the overnight range, used as a sweep level and as an objective.

settings.label: Regular trading hours
settings.html: Regular trading hours. Its first bar restarts the RTH VWAP and the opening range.

settings.label: Signal window
settings.html: The only window in which a zone touch may become a trade. Outside it, touches are still scored and reported as candidates.

settings.label: Maximum active trades
settings.html: How many trades may be open at once. A qualifying touch is ignored while this many are active.

settings.label: Show past trades
settings.html: Keep finished trades on the chart for the past-trade retention hours instead of the short default retention.

settings.label: Past-trade retention hours
settings.html: How many hours a finished trade stays drawn when Show past trades is on.

settings.label: Default completed-trade retention
settings.html: How many minutes a finished trade stays drawn when Show past trades is off.

settings.label: Engine history bars
settings.html: The number of newest bars the engine is meant to walk. This study walks every bar on the chart, so the setting has no effect here.

settings.label: Chart-timeframe zones
settings.html: Collect Fair Value Gaps and Order Blocks from the chart timeframe itself, not only from the higher buckets.

settings.label: 5-minute
settings.html: Collect zones from 5-minute buckets folded from the chart bars.

settings.label: 15-minute
settings.html: Collect zones from 15-minute buckets folded from the chart bars.

settings.label: 30-minute
settings.html: Collect zones from 30-minute buckets folded from the chart bars.

settings.label: 1-hour
settings.html: Collect zones from 1-hour buckets folded from the chart bars.

settings.label: 4-hour
settings.html: Collect zones from 4-hour buckets folded from the chart bars.

settings.label: 1m/chart zone maximum life
settings.html: The longest a chart-timeframe zone stays active, in minutes from the bar that confirmed it.

settings.label: 5m zone maximum life
settings.html: The longest a 5-minute zone stays active, in minutes.

settings.label: 15m zone maximum life
settings.html: The longest a 15-minute zone stays active, in minutes.

settings.label: 30m zone maximum life
settings.html: The longest a 30-minute zone stays active, in minutes.

settings.label: 1H zone maximum life
settings.html: The longest a 1-hour zone stays active, in minutes.

settings.label: 4H zones last until futures-session close
settings.html: Keep 4-hour zones active until 17:00 in the session timezone (at least two minutes), instead of using the fixed 4H life.

settings.label: 4H fallback maximum life
settings.html: The longest a 4-hour zone stays active, in minutes, when 4H zones do not run to the session close.

settings.label: Zone lifetime mode
settings.html: Fixed by timeframe gives every zone its full life. Shorten weaker zones cuts the life to three quarters for a moderate score and to half for a weak one.

settings.label: IFVG / BB lifetime (% of source zone)
settings.html: The life of an Inversion FVG or Breaker Block, as a percentage of the life its source zone would get, counted from the candle that flipped it.

settings.label: Full-life score
settings.html: The score at which a zone keeps its full life in the shortening mode.

settings.label: Three-quarter-life score
settings.html: The score at which a zone keeps three quarters of its life in the shortening mode. A new zone is also timed with at least this score.

settings.label: Fair Value Gaps
settings.html: Register Fair Value Gaps: a gap between the high of one candle and the low of the candle two later.

settings.label: Inversion FVGs
settings.html: Flip a Fair Value Gap into an Inversion FVG of the opposite direction when price closes through it.

settings.label: Order Blocks
settings.html: Register Order Blocks: the last opposite candle before a displacement candle that breaks the recent structure.

settings.label: Breaker Blocks
settings.html: Flip an Order Block into a Breaker Block of the opposite direction when price closes through it.

settings.label: Minimum zone width (ticks)
settings.html: The narrowest zone accepted, in price ticks taken from the chart.

settings.label: Minimum zone size / source ATR
settings.html: The narrowest zone accepted, as a multiple of the ATR of the timeframe it came from.

settings.label: Maximum zone size / source ATR
settings.html: The widest zone accepted, as a multiple of the ATR of the timeframe it came from.

settings.label: HTF displacement body / ATR
settings.html: How large a candle body must be, in ATRs, to count as displacement when finding Order Blocks.

settings.label: HTF displacement body fraction
settings.html: How much of its range a candle body must fill to count as displacement when finding Order Blocks.

settings.label: HTF structure lookback
settings.html: How many earlier candles the displacement close must clear to count as a break of structure for an Order Block.

settings.label: Pivot left
settings.html: Bars to the left a swing high or low must exceed. Swings feed the structure breaks and the liquidity pools.

settings.label: Pivot right
settings.html: Bars to the right a swing must exceed, which is also how many bars late each swing is confirmed.

settings.label: Immediate structure-event bars
settings.html: For how many bars a break of structure counts as recent for scoring.

settings.label: Same-leg structure validity minutes
settings.html: For how many minutes a break of structure counts as recent for scoring.

settings.label: Displacement validity minutes
settings.html: For how many minutes a displacement candle on the chart counts as recent for scoring.

settings.label: Execution displacement body / ATR
settings.html: How large a chart candle body must be, in ATRs, to count as displacement for scoring.

settings.label: Execution body fraction
settings.html: How much of its range a chart candle body must fill to count as displacement for scoring.

settings.label: Repeated-wick liquidity pools
settings.html: Group repeated swing highs and lows at nearly the same price into liquidity pools, and score zones near them.

settings.label: Pool tolerance in ticks
settings.html: How close, in ticks, a new swing must be to an existing pool to join it.

settings.label: Minimum pool touches
settings.html: How many swings a pool needs before it is drawn, scored or used as an objective.

settings.label: Pool lookback bars
settings.html: How many bars a pool may go without a new touch before it is dropped.

settings.label: Pool break confirmation ticks
settings.html: How far, in ticks, a close must go through a pool to break it rather than sweep it.

settings.label: Use liquidity pools as trade objectives
settings.html: Count the nearest pool in the trade direction as an objective when checking the room to the target.

settings.label: Liquidity-event validity bars
settings.html: For how many bars a sweep of a pool or a fixed level counts as recent for scoring.

settings.label: Opening Range minutes
settings.html: The length of the opening range that starts at 09:30 in the session timezone.

settings.label: Session and RTH VWAP
settings.html: Award context points when price rejects the session or RTH VWAP in the zone direction.

settings.label: RSI
settings.html: Award a context point when the RSI turns in the zone direction.

settings.label: RSI length
settings.html: The RSI length, used on the chart and on every higher bucket.

settings.label: Rolling z-score
settings.html: Award a context point when the close turns back from a stretched z-score.

settings.label: Z-score length
settings.html: How many closes the z-score mean and standard deviation cover.

settings.label: Z-score extreme
settings.html: How far, in standard deviations, the close must have been before a turn counts.

settings.label: Power-of-three session proxy
settings.html: Award an intermarket point when a sweep of a fixed level closes back on the right side of the session VWAP.

settings.label: Opening Range breakout/retest
settings.html: Award an intermarket point for a break and retest of the completed opening range.

settings.label: Same-time relative volume
settings.html: Use volume against the same time of day in earlier sessions in the context score.

settings.label: RVOL baseline sessions
settings.html: How many earlier sessions the same-time volume average covers.

settings.label: RVOL minimum samples
settings.html: How many earlier sessions are needed before relative volume is computed.

settings.label: Elevated RVOL
settings.html: The relative volume at which volume counts as elevated.

settings.label: Signal minimum score
settings.html: The score out of 100 a zone needs before a touch can become a trade.

settings.label: Minimum independent categories
settings.html: How many scoring categories must count before a touch can become a trade. The zone itself always counts, structure counts from 10 points, and every other category counts as soon as it awards a point.

settings.label: Require recent BOS/MSS
settings.html: Only trade a zone while a break of structure in its direction is recent.

settings.label: Require recent displacement
settings.html: Only trade a zone while a displacement candle in its direction is recent.

settings.label: Maximum zone touches before entry
settings.html: The most separate touches a zone may have had and still be traded.

settings.label: One trade per structural leg
settings.html: Allow only one trade per direction for each leg between breaks of structure.

settings.label: Same-direction cooldown bars
settings.html: How many bars must pass after a trade before another one in the same direction.

settings.label: Minimum space to objective in R
settings.html: The least room, in multiples of the risk, between the entry and the nearest objective level.

settings.label: Entry mode
settings.html: First touch enters on any bar that reaches the zone. Midpoint reclaim needs the bar to cross the midpoint and close back. Rejection close needs a close beyond the midpoint with a candle in the trade direction.

settings.label: ATR length
settings.html: The ATR length, used on the chart and on every higher bucket.

settings.label: Invalidation buffer ticks
settings.html: How many ticks beyond the far edge of the zone the stop is placed.

settings.label: Stop-size limits
settings.html: Automatic caps the stop at 32 ticks (12 on ES and MES), Custom uses the custom cap, and Off removes the size checks.

settings.label: Custom maximum stop ticks
settings.html: The largest stop, in ticks, allowed in Custom mode.

settings.label: Maximum stop / ATR
settings.html: The largest stop allowed, as a multiple of the chart ATR, unless the limits are off.

settings.label: Trade drawing duration
settings.html: How long a trade runs before it is closed at the time limit.

settings.label: Maximum retained trades
settings.html: The most trades kept for drawing; the oldest are dropped first.

settings.label: Setup-zone transparency
settings.html: Transparency of the zone box drawn behind an open trade.

settings.label: Risk transparency
settings.html: Transparency of the band between the entry and the stop.

settings.label: Entry-to-1R transparency
settings.html: Transparency of the band between the entry and 1R.

settings.label: 1R-to-1.5R transparency
settings.html: Transparency of the band between 1R and 1.5R.

settings.label: 1.5R-to-2R transparency
settings.html: Transparency of the band between 1.5R and 2R.

settings.label: Historical-trade transparency
settings.html: Transparency of every band of a finished trade.

settings.label: Stop/target line width
settings.html: Thickness of the stop and objective lines.

settings.label: Show multi-timeframe regime panel
settings.html: Show the table of regimes for every timeframe, the engine status and the latest candidate.

settings.label: Regime table position
settings.html: The corner the panel was meant to sit in. The panel here always sits in the bottom-right corner.

settings.label: Regime table text size
settings.html: The panel text size that was meant to be used. The panel here uses the chart text size.

settings.label: Show scores in zone labels
settings.html: Add the current score to each zone label.

settings.label: Zone label placement
settings.html: Put zone labels inside the right end of the box, or above its right edge.

settings.label: Liquidity label offset (ticks)
settings.html: How many ticks the pool labels sit away from their lines.

settings.label: Show active research zones
settings.html: Draw the active zones and their labels, newest first.

settings.label: Research zone filter
settings.html: Relevant only draws zones that score at least the candidate minimum or lie within four ATRs of the price. All active draws every active zone.

settings.label: Show active liquidity-pool lines
settings.html: Draw dashed lines for up to eight active pools that have enough touches.

settings.label: Liquidity-line forward projection
settings.html: How many minutes past the newest bar the pool lines reach.

settings.label: Show recently invalidated zones
settings.html: Keep a zone that price closed through on the chart, up to its invalidation candle, for the retention period.

settings.label: Invalidated-zone history retention
settings.html: How many minutes an invalidated zone stays drawn.

settings.label: Maximum visible research zones
settings.html: The most zones drawn at once.

settings.label: Research candidate minimum
settings.html: The score at which a touched zone counts as a candidate, for the filter and the candidate labels.

settings.label: Show rejected touched candidates
settings.html: Label each touched candidate that did not become a trade with its score and the first gate it failed.

settings.label: Enable alerts
settings.html: Turn every alert of this study on or off.

settings.label: BUY / SELL signal
settings.html: Raise an alert when a BUY or SELL trade opens.

settings.label: Target reached
settings.html: Raise an alert when a trade reaches 2R.

settings.label: Stop reached
settings.html: Raise an alert when a trade reaches its stop.

faq.q: Why does the panel say USE 1M or CHECK SYMBOL, with nothing drawn?
faq.html: The zone and trade engine runs only on a 1-minute chart (or up to 5 minutes with that option on) of an instrument whose ticker starts with NQ, MNQ, ES or MES. USE 1M means the instrument is fine but the timeframe is not; CHECK SYMBOL means the instrument is not one of those. Turn on Allow symbols other than NQ/ES to run it on another instrument.

faq.q: Where do the higher-timeframe zones come from?
faq.html: From the chart itself. The 1-minute bars are grouped into 5, 15, 30, 60 and 240 minute buckets that start at the futures session open, and a bucket's zones are released on the first bar of the next bucket, once the bucket has closed.

faq.q: Why did a strong-looking touch not become a trade?
faq.html: Every gate must pass at once, and only the best qualifying zone on a bar is taken. Turn on Show rejected touched candidates to label each candidate with the first gate it failed, such as Score/categories, No structure or Outside signal window.

faq.q: What decides the stop and the targets?
faq.html: The stop sits a few ticks beyond the far edge of the zone, and its size must stay inside the stop limits. The risk from the entry close to the stop sets the 1R, 1.5R and 2R objectives.

futures-setups-research.deviation: The regime panel always sits in the bottom-right corner at the chart's text size, because a table's corner is fixed before the first bar and a table has no text size; the zone engine walks every bar rather than only the newest Engine history bars, and on a chart that gives no tick size the fallback tick is taken from the latest 50 closes so far rather than the chart's final 50, because a study that runs bar by bar cannot see which bar will be the newest; and a session timezone name the chart does not know stops the study instead of falling back to America/New_York, because a zone name cannot be tested before it is used.

futures-setups.title: Futures Setups
futures-setups.summary: Scores Fair Value Gaps and Order Blocks from six timeframes out of 100 and turns the best qualifying touch into a trade plan with a stop and 1R, 1.5R and 2R targets.
futures-setups.descriptionHtml:
Futures Setups records supply and demand zones on the chart timeframe and on 5, 15, 30, 60 and 240 minute bars that it builds from the chart's own bars, counted from the 18:00 session open in the session timezone. A zone is a Fair Value Gap (a three-bar gap between the first bar and the third) or an Order Block (the last opposite-colour bar before a displacement bar that closes through the recent high or low). A higher-timeframe zone is only read from closed bars, so it appears when its bar has finished. When price closes through a zone, the gap becomes an Inversion FVG and the block a Breaker Block facing the other way, each with a shorter life of its own.

Every open zone is scored out of 100 on each bar across six categories: zone authority (its timeframe, type and width, up to 30), multi-timeframe overlap with other open zones on the same side (up to 25), structure (a recent break of structure or market structure shift and a recent displacement bar, up to 20), liquidity (recent sweeps of liquidity pools, the previous day, the previous week, the overnight range and the opening range, and pools or levels near the zone, up to 15), market context (VWAP, the weighted regime, z-score, RSI and relative volume, up to 10) and session behaviour (a power-of-three sweep or an opening-range break, up to 4).

When a zone is touched in the signal window and passes every gate (score, number of categories, structure, displacement, touch count, cooldown, stop size and room to the nearest objective), the study opens a trade plan at the close: a stop a few ticks beyond the zone and targets at 1R, 1.5R and 2R. The plan finishes at its stop, at 2R or when its time runs out. A regime panel scores the trend of every timeframe from -100 to 100 using its averages, VWAP, RSI, momentum and volume.
futures-setups.howToReadHtml:
Start with the regime panel in the bottom-right corner. Each timeframe reads STRONG BULL, BULLISH, BALANCED, BEARISH or STRONG BEAR with its score, and setups that agree with the higher timeframes score more. ENGINE reads READY when the setup engine is running; it only runs on NQ, MNQ, ES and MES one-minute charts unless the two switches in Quick Start are on, and otherwise the panel is all the study shows.

A trade plan is drawn as a BUY or SELL plate with its score at the entry, the zone it came from, a red risk box down to the STOP line and green boxes to the 1R, 1.5R and 2R lines. When the plan finishes, a label shows how: STOP -1R, TARGET +2R or a TIME exit. The score is a checklist of conditions, not a probability, and a plan that reaches 1R and then times out is not a loss or a win in itself. Read it on real, latest market data, and treat the plans as candidates to review rather than orders.

settings.label: Enable indicator
settings.html: Master switch for zone registration. Off, no zones are recorded, so no zone is scored and no trade plan is drawn; the regime panel still updates.

settings.label: Allow symbols other than NQ/ES
settings.html: The engine runs only when the symbol's leading letters are NQ, MNQ, ES or MES (or the chart names no symbol) unless this is on. Turn it on to run the setup engine on any other instrument.

settings.label: Allow chart timeframes above 1 minute
settings.html: The engine only runs on a one-minute chart unless this is on. On, it also runs on charts of two to five minutes.

settings.label: Session timezone
settings.html: The timezone every session window, the 18:00 trading-day boundary and the 09:30 opening range are read in. It must be a full zone name such as America/New_York; a name the chart does not recognise stops the study.

settings.label: Futures session
settings.html: The futures trading session, written HHMM-HHMM with an optional list of days (1 is Sunday, 7 is Saturday). The session VWAP and the same-time volume slots run inside it.

settings.label: Overnight session
settings.html: The overnight window whose high and low become reference levels for sweeps and objectives.

settings.label: Regular trading hours
settings.html: Regular trading hours. Its first bar resets the RTH VWAP and starts the opening range.

settings.label: Signal window
settings.html: Trade plans are only opened inside this window. Widen it to allow overnight or evening signals.

settings.label: Maximum active trades
settings.html: The most trade plans that can be open at the same time. A new plan waits until one of them finishes.

settings.label: Show past trades
settings.html: Keep finished trade plans on the chart for the retention hours below instead of the short default retention.

settings.label: Past-trade retention hours
settings.html: How long a finished trade plan stays on the chart when past trades are shown.

settings.label: Default completed-trade retention
settings.html: How long a finished trade plan stays on the chart when past trades are not shown.

settings.label: Chart-timeframe zones
settings.html: Record Fair Value Gaps and Order Blocks found on the chart timeframe itself.

settings.label: 5-minute zones
settings.html: Record zones from 5-minute bars built out of the chart bars.

settings.label: 15-minute zones
settings.html: Record zones from 15-minute bars built out of the chart bars.

settings.label: 30-minute zones
settings.html: Record zones from 30-minute bars built out of the chart bars.

settings.label: 1-hour zones
settings.html: Record zones from 1-hour bars built out of the chart bars.

settings.label: 4-hour zones
settings.html: Record zones from 4-hour bars built out of the chart bars, counted from the 18:00 session open.

settings.label: 1m/chart zone maximum life
settings.html: How many minutes a chart-timeframe zone stays open before it expires.

settings.label: 5m zone maximum life
settings.html: How many minutes a 5-minute zone stays open before it expires.

settings.label: 15m zone maximum life
settings.html: How many minutes a 15-minute zone stays open before it expires.

settings.label: 30m zone maximum life
settings.html: How many minutes a 30-minute zone stays open before it expires.

settings.label: 1H zone maximum life
settings.html: How many minutes a 1-hour zone stays open before it expires.

settings.label: 4H zones last until futures-session close
settings.html: On, a 4-hour zone stays open until the next 17:00 session close (at least two minutes). Off, it uses the fallback life below.

settings.label: 4H fallback maximum life
settings.html: How many minutes a 4-hour zone stays open when it is not held to the session close.

settings.label: Zone lifetime mode
settings.html: Fixed by timeframe gives every zone its full life. Shorten weaker zones cuts the life to three quarters below the full-life score and to half below the three-quarter-life score.

settings.label: IFVG / BB lifetime (% of source zone)
settings.html: The life of an Inversion FVG or a Breaker Block, as a percentage of the life its source zone had, counted from the bar that flipped it.

settings.label: Full-life score
settings.html: In the shortening mode, a zone scoring at least this keeps its full life.

settings.label: Three-quarter-life score
settings.html: In the shortening mode, a zone scoring at least this keeps three quarters of its life. A new zone's first expiry also assumes at least this score.

settings.label: Fair Value Gaps
settings.html: Record Fair Value Gaps: a three-bar gap between the first bar's high and the third bar's low, or the reverse.

settings.label: Inversion FVGs
settings.html: When price closes through a Fair Value Gap, record the same range as an Inversion FVG facing the other way.

settings.label: Order Blocks
settings.html: Record Order Blocks: the last opposite-colour bar before a displacement bar that closes beyond the recent high or low.

settings.label: Breaker Blocks
settings.html: When price closes through an Order Block, record the same range as a Breaker Block facing the other way.

settings.label: Minimum zone width (ticks)
settings.html: A zone narrower than this many price ticks is ignored. The tick is the instrument's tick size; when the chart states none, a tick of 0.01 is used.

settings.label: Minimum zone size / source ATR
settings.html: A zone narrower than this fraction of its source timeframe's ATR is ignored.

settings.label: Maximum zone size / source ATR
settings.html: A zone wider than this multiple of its source timeframe's ATR is ignored.

settings.label: HTF displacement body / ATR
settings.html: The body a bar needs, as a multiple of ATR, to count as displacement when finding Order Blocks.

settings.label: HTF displacement body fraction
settings.html: The share of the bar's range its body must fill to count as displacement when finding Order Blocks.

settings.label: HTF structure lookback
settings.html: How many bars back the high or low is taken from when testing whether a displacement bar broke structure.

settings.label: Pivot left
settings.html: Bars to the left a swing high or low must stand beyond.

settings.label: Pivot right
settings.html: Bars to the right a swing high or low must stand beyond, which is also how many bars late a swing is confirmed.

settings.label: Immediate structure-event bars
settings.html: A break of structure counts as recent for this many bars after it.

settings.label: Same-leg structure validity minutes
settings.html: A break of structure also counts as recent for this many minutes after it.

settings.label: Displacement validity minutes
settings.html: A displacement bar on the chart counts as recent for this many minutes after it.

settings.label: Execution displacement body / ATR
settings.html: The body a chart bar needs, as a multiple of ATR, to count as execution displacement.

settings.label: Execution body fraction
settings.html: The share of the range a chart bar's body must fill to count as execution displacement.

settings.label: Repeated-wick liquidity pools
settings.html: Group swing highs and lows at a similar price into liquidity pools, and score their sweeps and their nearness to a zone.

settings.label: Pool tolerance in ticks
settings.html: How close, in ticks, a new swing must be to an existing pool to join it.

settings.label: Minimum pool touches
settings.html: How many swings a pool needs before it counts.

settings.label: Pool lookback bars
settings.html: A pool closes when no swing has touched it for this many bars.

settings.label: Pool break confirmation ticks
settings.html: A close this many ticks beyond a pool breaks it rather than sweeping it.

settings.label: Use liquidity pools as trade objectives
settings.html: Include the nearest qualified pool beyond the entry when measuring the room to the first objective.

settings.label: Liquidity-event validity bars
settings.html: A sweep of a pool or of a reference level counts as recent for this many bars.

settings.label: Opening Range minutes
settings.html: The length of the opening range measured from 09:30 in the session timezone.

settings.label: Session and RTH VWAP
settings.html: Score a zone higher when price rejects the session or RTH VWAP in the zone's direction, or the VWAP sits inside the zone.

settings.label: RSI
settings.html: Score a zone higher when RSI turns in the zone's direction.

settings.label: RSI length
settings.html: The RSI length, used for the context points and the regime scores.

settings.label: Rolling z-score
settings.html: Score a zone higher when a stretched close turns back towards its mean.

settings.label: Z-score length
settings.html: How many bars the rolling mean and standard deviation of the close cover.

settings.label: Z-score extreme
settings.html: How many standard deviations from the mean counts as stretched.

settings.label: Power-of-three session proxy
settings.html: Score a zone higher when a reference level is swept and price closes back on the session VWAP side the zone favours.

settings.label: Opening Range breakout/retest
settings.html: Score a zone higher on a close beyond the completed opening range that retests it.

settings.label: Same-time relative volume
settings.html: Score a zone higher when volume is elevated against the same time of day in earlier sessions.

settings.label: RVOL baseline sessions
settings.html: How many earlier sessions the same-time volume average covers.

settings.label: RVOL minimum samples
settings.html: How many earlier sessions are needed before relative volume is reported.

settings.label: Elevated RVOL
settings.html: The relative volume that counts as elevated, for scoring and for the regime.

settings.label: Signal minimum score
settings.html: A zone must score at least this out of 100 before a trade plan can open from it.

settings.label: Minimum independent categories
settings.html: A zone must score in at least this many of the six categories before a trade plan can open from it.

settings.label: Require recent BOS/MSS
settings.html: Only open a trade plan when a break of structure in the zone's direction is recent.

settings.label: Require recent displacement
settings.html: Only open a trade plan when a displacement bar in the zone's direction is recent.

settings.label: Maximum zone touches before entry
settings.html: A zone touched more times than this can no longer open a trade plan.

settings.label: One trade per structural leg
settings.html: Allow only one trade plan per direction for each leg between breaks of structure.

settings.label: Same-direction cooldown bars
settings.html: Bars to wait after a trade plan before another one in the same direction.

settings.label: Minimum space to objective in R
settings.html: The nearest objective beyond the entry must be at least this many times the risk away. Zero turns the test off.

settings.label: Entry mode
settings.html: What a touch must do to open a trade plan: First touch enters on any touch, Midpoint reclaim needs a close back across the midpoint, Rejection close needs a close beyond the midpoint in a candle of the trade's colour.

settings.label: ATR length
settings.html: The ATR length used for zone sizes, displacement, stop limits and the regime.

settings.label: Invalidation buffer ticks
settings.html: The stop sits this many ticks beyond the far edge of the zone.

settings.label: Stop-size limits
settings.html: Automatic caps the stop at 12 ticks on ES and MES and 32 ticks elsewhere, Custom uses the cap below, Off removes the caps. With a cap, a stop must also be at least 2 ticks and no wider than the ATR limit below.

settings.label: Custom maximum stop ticks
settings.html: The largest stop, in ticks, when the stop-size limits are Custom.

settings.label: Maximum stop / ATR
settings.html: The largest stop as a multiple of ATR, when stop-size limits are on.

settings.label: Trade drawing duration
settings.html: A trade plan that has not reached its stop or 2R by this many minutes is closed on time.

settings.label: Maximum retained trades
settings.html: The most trade plans, open and finished, the chart keeps.

settings.label: Show multi-timeframe regime panel
settings.html: Show the regime table with the six timeframe regimes, the engine state, the threshold and the latest candidate.

settings.label: Regime table position
settings.html: Kept for compatibility with saved settings. This version always pins the panel to the bottom-right corner.

settings.label: Regime table text size
settings.html: Kept for compatibility with saved settings. This version draws the panel at the chart's own table text size.

settings.label: Show scores in zone labels
settings.html: Add each zone's current score to its label in the research view.

settings.label: Zone label placement
settings.html: Inside right puts a zone label at its midpoint near the right edge; Above right puts it just above the zone's top edge.

settings.label: Liquidity label offset (ticks)
settings.html: How far, in ticks, pool labels sit from their line: below a support pool, above a resistance pool.

settings.label: Research build
settings.html: Off by default, which hides every research drawing below. On, the research options take effect.

settings.label: Show active research zones
settings.html: In the research view, draw the open zones (and recently invalidated ones) as boxes with labels.

settings.label: Research zone filter
settings.html: Relevant only draws zones that score at least the research candidate minimum or sit within four ATRs of price; All active draws every open zone.

settings.label: Show active liquidity-pool lines
settings.html: In the research view, draw up to eight qualified pools as dashed lines projected past the latest bar.

settings.label: Liquidity-line forward projection
settings.html: How many minutes past the latest bar the pool lines extend.

settings.label: Show recently invalidated zones
settings.html: In the research view, keep a zone that price closed through visible up to the bar that invalidated it.

settings.label: Invalidated-zone history retention
settings.html: How long an invalidated zone stays in the research view.

settings.label: Maximum visible research zones
settings.html: The most zones the research view draws, newest first.

settings.label: Research candidate minimum
settings.html: The score a touched zone needs to be marked as a candidate in the research view.

settings.label: Show rejected touched candidates
settings.html: In the research view, label touched candidates that did not qualify, with the reason they failed.

settings.label: Enable alerts
settings.html: Master switch for the four alerts below.

settings.label: BUY / SELL signal
settings.html: Alert when a BUY or SELL trade plan opens.

settings.label: Target reached
settings.html: Alert when a trade plan reaches its 2R target.

settings.label: Stop reached
settings.html: Alert when a trade plan reaches its stop.

faq.q: Why does the chart only show the regime panel?
faq.html: The setup engine runs only on NQ, MNQ, ES and MES symbols on a one-minute chart by default. Turn on "Allow symbols other than NQ/ES" for another instrument, and "Allow chart timeframes above 1 minute" for a chart of two to five minutes. Above five minutes the engine stays off and only the regime panel updates.

faq.q: Why does a 4-hour zone appear long after the gap formed?
faq.html: Higher-timeframe bars are built from the chart's bars and a zone is read only once its bar has closed, so a 4-hour gap is recorded on the first chart bar after its third 4-hour bar finishes. Nothing is read from a bar that is still forming.

faq.q: What do the six categories add up to?
faq.html: Zone authority gives up to 30 points, overlap up to 25, structure up to 20, liquidity up to 15, market context up to 10 and session behaviour up to 4, capped at 100. The default threshold needs a score of 80 spread over at least four categories.

faq.q: What are the columns such as Weighted Regime and Latest Candidate Score?
faq.html: They are readings the study keeps for the data window and are not drawn: the entry, stop and targets on the bar a plan opens, the weighted and chart-timeframe regime scores on every bar, and the score of the best zone price touched most recently.

futures-setups.deviation: When the chart states no tick size, the original infers one from the median bar range of the whole chart, later bars included, which a study computed bar by bar cannot see; this version then uses a tick of 0.01, so its tick-based zone widths, pool tolerances, stop buffer and stop caps differ on such a chart.

options-context.title: Options Context
options-context.summary: An intraday context score from -100 to 100 that blends trend, session structure, momentum, volume, persistence and higher timeframes, with a confidence line.
options-context.descriptionHtml:
Options Context grades the intraday backdrop on one scale. Six components are each scored from -100 (strongly bearish) to +100 (strongly bullish): trend (the gap and slope of a fast and a slow EMA, in ATR), structure (the close against the session VWAP, the session open and the opening range), momentum (a volatility-normalized log return, its recent change and RSI), participation (where the bar closed and its one-bar return, weighted by relative volume), persistence (how consistently recent regular-session bars closed on one side of VWAP, closed up or down from the previous close, and had the fast EMA on one side of the slow EMA) and the higher timeframes.

Every distance is divided by ATR and passed through a soft saturation, x / (1 + |x|), so no single reading can run away. Relative volume compares each regular-session bar with the same slot of the previous sessions, both for the bar alone and for the volume so far today. The 1H, 4H, daily and weekly readings are folded from the chart's own bars, with intraday buckets anchored to the first bar of each day, and every chart bar reads the last closed higher-timeframe bar, so a reading never changes after the fact.

Context Direction is the weighted mean of the components that exist on the bar. Confidence, from 0 to 100, is a weighted blend of four things: how strongly and how consistently the components agree, the volume intensity behind the participation score, a volatility term that is highest when the volatility reading sits near 65, and the size of the persistence score. Direction is then latched into seven regimes, from strong bear to strong bull, with hysteresis: a regime is held on a weaker score than the one that entered it, so it does not flip back and forth around a threshold. The regime colours the line and shades the background.
options-context.howToReadHtml:
Read the line as a bias, not a signal. Above +20 the context leans bullish, above +45 it is bullish and above +75 strongly so; the same levels below zero read bearish. The Confidence line says how much to trust that bias: below 35 the components disagree or volume is thin, and the dashboard's Levels Bias then reads LOW CONVICTION. With confidence of 35 or more, Levels Bias reads PREFER SUPPORT at +45 and above (SUPPORT LEAN from +20), PREFER RESISTANCE at -45 and below (RESISTANCE LEAN from -20) and TWO-SIDED in between, which is the side of the market the context favours working from.

The columns show relative volume scaled to the display cap, tinted by whether participation was buying or selling. Structure, participation and persistence only exist inside the regular session, so outside it the blend rests on trend, momentum and the higher timeframes. The opening range only counts on charts whose bars are no longer than the range. The score describes the latest bars; it does not forecast, and on a market that trades around the clock the session you choose decides what counts as the open.

settings.label: Session timezone
settings.html: The IANA zone the regular session, the day boundaries and the week boundaries are read in, such as America/New_York or Asia/Kolkata. A blank field reads New York time; a name that is not a timezone stops the script with an error.

settings.label: Regular session
settings.html: The regular session as two HHMM clock times joined by a hyphen, on the wall clock of the session timezone. An end before the start crosses midnight. An unreadable value falls back to 0930-1600.

settings.label: Monday-Friday only
settings.html: When on, only Monday to Friday bars count as regular-session bars. Turn it off for an instrument that also trades at the weekend.

settings.label: Opening-range minutes
settings.html: How long the opening range lasts from the first regular-session bar. The range is ignored when a chart bar is longer than this.

settings.label: ATR length
settings.html: The average true range that every distance in the trend, structure and momentum scores is measured in.

settings.label: Fast EMA
settings.html: Length of the fast exponential average used by the trend score, the persistence score and the legacy vote.

settings.label: Slow EMA
settings.html: Length of the slow exponential average the fast one is compared with.

settings.label: Slope lookback
settings.html: How many bars back the slope of each average is measured over.

settings.label: EMA spread scale (ATR)
settings.html: The gap between the two averages, in ATR, that scores about half way to the extreme. Larger values make the trend score less sensitive.

settings.label: EMA slope scale (ATR)
settings.html: The slope of an average, in ATR, that scores about half way to the extreme.

settings.label: RTH VWAP source
settings.html: The price the session VWAP is built from.

settings.label: VWAP displacement scale (ATR)
settings.html: The distance from the session VWAP, in ATR, that scores about half way to the extreme in the structure score.

settings.label: Opening-range break scale (ATR)
settings.html: How far past the opening range, in ATR, a close must sit before the break score approaches its extreme.

settings.label: RTH-open displacement scale (ATR)
settings.html: The distance from the session open, in ATR, that scores about half way to the extreme.

settings.label: RSI source
settings.html: The price the RSI in the momentum score is computed on.

settings.label: RSI length
settings.html: Length of the RSI on the chart, and of the RSI inside every higher-timeframe reading.

settings.label: Normalized-return lookback
settings.html: How many bars back the log return in the momentum score is measured over.

settings.label: Normalized-return scale
settings.html: The volatility-normalized return that scores about half way to the extreme. Larger values damp the momentum score.

settings.label: Momentum-change lookback
settings.html: How many bars back the change in the return score is measured over.

settings.label: Momentum-change scale
settings.html: The change in the return score that scores about half way to the extreme.

settings.label: RVOL historical days
settings.html: How many earlier sessions the relative volume compares each bar with, slot by slot.

settings.label: Directional-return scale (ATR)
settings.html: The one-bar return, in ATR terms, that counts about half way to a full directional push in the participation score.

settings.label: RVOL intensity scale
settings.html: How quickly volume above normal turns into participation intensity. Larger values need more volume for the same intensity.

settings.label: High RVOL threshold
settings.html: Relative volume at or above this is high: it casts a legacy vote, is marked in the dashboard and can raise the aligned volume alert.

settings.label: Extreme RVOL threshold
settings.html: Relative volume at or above this is labelled extreme in the dashboard.

settings.label: RVOL display cap
settings.html: The relative volume that fills a column to 100. Higher values are drawn at 100.

settings.label: Persistence bars
settings.html: How many bars the persistence score averages its three side votes over.

settings.label: Short ATR length
settings.html: The fast average true range in the volatility ratio.

settings.label: Long ATR length
settings.html: The slow average true range the fast one is divided by.

settings.label: Volatility history
settings.html: How many bars of the volatility ratio its mean and standard deviation are taken over.

settings.label: Volatility z-score scale
settings.html: The z-score that moves the volatility reading about half way from 50 to its extreme.

settings.label: Include HTF trend in Context
settings.html: When on, the higher-timeframe composite joins the blend with weight 0.15 and the local weights are scaled to 85 percent.

settings.label: Show 1H / 4H / 1D / 1W states
settings.html: Adds the two rows with each higher timeframe's score and state to the detailed dashboard.

settings.label: HTF fast EMA
settings.html: Length of the fast average on each folded higher timeframe.

settings.label: HTF slow EMA
settings.html: Length of the slow average on each folded higher timeframe. A daily or weekly reading needs this many closed days or weeks before it appears.

settings.label: HTF ATR length
settings.html: The average true range each higher timeframe's distances are measured in.

settings.label: HTF EMA slope bars
settings.html: How many higher-timeframe bars back the slope of each average is measured over.

settings.label: HTF recent-path bars
settings.html: How many higher-timeframe bars the path return and path efficiency look back over.

settings.label: HTF persistence bars
settings.html: How many higher-timeframe bars the balance of closes above and below the fast average is taken over.

settings.label: HTF EMA spread scale (ATR)
settings.html: The gap between the higher-timeframe averages, in ATR, that scores about half way to the extreme.

settings.label: HTF EMA slope scale (ATR/bar)
settings.html: The slope per bar, in ATR, that scores about half way to the extreme on a higher timeframe.

settings.label: HTF path-return scale
settings.html: The path return, in ATR times the square root of the path length, that scores about half way to the extreme.

settings.label: HTF directional threshold
settings.html: How far from zero a higher-timeframe score must be to count as bullish or bearish in the dashboard's breadth count.

settings.label: Show Context Direction
settings.html: Draws the Context Direction line and its shading to zero.

settings.label: Show Context Confidence
settings.html: Draws the Confidence line.

settings.label: Show RVOL columns
settings.html: Draws the relative volume columns, coloured by the sign of the participation score.

settings.label: Show RSI momentum score
settings.html: Draws the RSI part of the momentum score on the same -100 to 100 scale.

settings.label: Show HTF composite
settings.html: Draws the weighted higher-timeframe composite.

settings.label: Subtle regime background
settings.html: Shades each bar's background in the colour of the latched regime.

settings.label: Regime background transparency
settings.html: How transparent the regime shading is, from 85 to 100. At 100 nothing is shaded.

settings.label: Show dashboard
settings.html: Shows the table of readings for the newest bar.

settings.label: Dashboard mode
settings.html: Detailed lists every component, the higher timeframes, volume, volatility and session state. Compact keeps the summary, HTF, RVOL and volatility rows.

settings.label: Dashboard position
settings.html: The corner of the pane the dashboard sits in.

settings.label: Dashboard text size
settings.html: Kept so saved settings load. The table is drawn at the chart's own text size, so it changes nothing on this chart.

settings.label: Enable alert conditions
settings.html: Turns all eight alerts on or off.

settings.label: High-confidence direction threshold
settings.html: How far from zero Context Direction must be for the high-confidence alert.

settings.label: High-confidence confidence threshold
settings.html: The confidence the high-confidence alert also requires.

settings.label: Strong-regime failure window (bars)
settings.html: How many bars after entering a strong regime a fall back through 20 (or a rise back through -20) counts as a failure alert.

settings.label: Show v0.1 binary-score comparison
settings.html: Draws the older five-vote score, times 20, for comparison with the graded blend.

faq.q: Why are the daily and weekly readings blank on my chart?
faq.html: Each higher timeframe needs as many closed buckets as the HTF slow EMA length (50 by default) before it has a reading, so on an intraday chart with a few months of history the weekly reading, and sometimes the daily, stays empty. The composite uses whichever timeframes have a reading.

faq.q: Why does the line sometimes rest on fewer components?
faq.html: Structure, participation and persistence are only computed on regular-session bars, and participation also needs earlier sessions to compare volume with. A missing component drops out of the weighted mean and the remaining weights are rescaled.

faq.q: What does the regime add over the line itself?
faq.html: The regime is a latch with hysteresis. A strong bull state entered at 75 is kept until the score falls below 68, and a bull state entered at 45 is kept down to 38, so the colour and the background change on a real shift rather than on every wiggle around a threshold.

faq.q: Which session should I set for an instrument that trades around the clock?
faq.html: Set the hours you treat as the main session, in the zone you care about. The session decides the VWAP reset, the opening range, the relative-volume slots and where persistence counts, so a different window gives a different reading.
