options-levels.title: Options Levels
options-levels.summary: Scores session, swing, gap, round-number and VWAP levels into clusters and keeps one support and one resistance reaction zone, tracking how price behaves at each.
options-levels.descriptionHtml:
Options Levels gathers the reference prices intraday traders watch and turns them into two zones. The candidates are the previous day's high, low and close, the previous week's high and low, the premarket high and low, the finished opening range, the regular-session open, an unfilled opening gap, the session VWAP and, when switched on, its first deviation bands, an optional anchored VWAP from an event you name, optional ATR projections from the session open and the previous close, the nearest round numbers, and confirmed swing pivots. Every level farther from the close than the set number of daily ATRs is dropped.

Each remaining level gets a score from 0 to 100. The score blends a base weight for its kind of level (a swing pivot weighs more when the swing was larger), how recent it is, and, for most kinds, what happened on the earlier bars that touched it: how many touches there were, how far price moved away in the favourable direction compared with the adverse one, how many closes held on the right side, how large the move was in daily ATR, and how heavy volume was against its 20-bar average. The daily ATR is the average true range of finished calendar days in the session timezone, so it is known from the first bar of each day without reading ahead. Until enough finished days exist, the ATR of the chart's own bars stands in.

Levels sorted by price are merged into clusters when they sit within the cluster tolerance. A cluster's width comes from the weighted spread of its members, held between a minimum and a maximum half-width, and its strength rises with the scores of its members and with how many different kinds of level agree. The most actionable strong cluster below the close becomes the support zone and the one above becomes the resistance zone. A zone is replaced only when a clearly better cluster appears, it is dropped when it breaks or when the rebuilt clusters stop matching it, and its state moves through approaching, inside, rejecting, accepting, broken and flipped as the bars arrive.
options-levels.howToReadHtml:
The two boxes on the right of the chart are the active zones: teal for support below price and red for resistance above it, each labelled with its state. A thinner shaded band at the outer edge of a zone, marked BUY or SELL, appears when the zone's actionability reaches the edge setting. A zone turns gray on the bar it breaks and is dropped on the next bar, and a broken zone that price retests from the other side within the flip watch can come back as a flipped zone of the opposite kind. The amber box marks the opening-range window, and the purple line is the regular-session VWAP.

Read a zone as an area where earlier reactions suggest price may pause or turn, not as a promise that it will. Rejection means the bar entered the zone and closed clearly away from it, acceptance means closes are holding inside or through it, and a break needs either a close well beyond it or the set number of closes in a row beyond it. The zones are built from intraday sessions, so on a daily chart, or on an instrument whose hours do not match the session settings, the levels say much less. The dashboard repeats the zone prices, the nearest zone's state and the daily ATR.

settings.label: Session timezone
settings.html: The IANA zone the session windows, calendar days and weeks are read in, written as a full Area/Location name such as America/New_York, or UTC.

settings.label: Regular session
settings.html: The regular-session window as HHMM-HHMM; its first bar resets the VWAP, the session open and the opening range.

settings.label: Premarket session
settings.html: The premarket window as HHMM-HHMM; its high and low become candidate levels.

settings.label: Monday-Friday only
settings.html: Count only Monday to Friday as session days; switch it off for an instrument that also trades at the weekend.

settings.label: Opening-range minutes
settings.html: How long the opening range keeps forming after the regular-session open before it is finished.

settings.label: Display mode
settings.html: Reaction Zones shows the zones only, Zones + Key References adds the reference lines, and Legacy / Debug also adds the gap lines, the EMAs when switched on, the event VWAP and scoring rows.

settings.label: Show zone text
settings.html: Write the side and state inside each zone box and BUY or SELL on the edge boxes.

settings.label: Show compact dashboard
settings.html: Show the table with the zone prices, the nearest zone's state and the daily ATR.

settings.label: Zone history bars
settings.html: The most bars back a zone box starts, even when its zone was chosen earlier.

settings.label: Zone projection bars
settings.html: How many bars to the right of the newest bar the zone boxes extend.

settings.label: Show buy / sell edge zones
settings.html: Draw the thinner BUY band at the bottom of the support zone and SELL band at the top of the resistance zone.

settings.label: Edge zone minimum actionability
settings.html: The actionability a zone needs before its edge band is drawn.

settings.label: Edge zone height (% of parent zone)
settings.html: The edge band's height as a fraction of its zone's height.

settings.label: Highlight opening-range window
settings.html: Draw a box over the latest opening range from its first bar to the bar it finished.

settings.label: Confirmed daily ATR length
settings.html: Number of finished days in the daily ATR that scales every distance and width.

settings.label: Maximum candidate distance (daily ATR)
settings.html: Levels farther than this many daily ATRs from the close are not considered.

settings.label: Cluster tolerance (daily ATR)
settings.html: Levels closer than this fraction of the daily ATR are merged into one cluster.

settings.label: Minimum cluster tolerance (ticks)
settings.html: The smallest cluster tolerance, in price ticks.

settings.label: Minimum cluster tolerance (% as decimal)
settings.html: The smallest cluster tolerance as a fraction of the close.

settings.label: Minimum zone half-width (daily ATR)
settings.html: The narrowest a zone can be on each side of its centre, in daily ATR.

settings.label: Maximum zone half-width (daily ATR)
settings.html: The widest a zone can be on each side of its centre, in daily ATR.

settings.label: Minimum zone half-width (ticks)
settings.html: The narrowest half-width in price ticks, used when it is wider than the ATR minimum.

settings.label: Cluster dispersion multiplier
settings.html: Multiplies the weighted spread of a cluster's levels to set its zone half-width.

settings.label: Distance decay
settings.html: How quickly a cluster's actionability falls as it sits farther from the close.

settings.label: Zone switch margin
settings.html: How many points stronger or more actionable a new cluster must be to replace the current zone.

settings.label: Minimum zone strength
settings.html: Clusters weaker than this are never chosen as a zone.

settings.label: Cluster refresh bars
settings.html: Rebuild the clusters every this many bars, besides the rebuilds that sessions, pivots and breaks trigger.

settings.label: Approaching distance (daily ATR)
settings.html: A zone this close to the close, in daily ATR, is marked approaching.

settings.label: Rejection displacement (daily ATR)
settings.html: How far beyond a zone the close must land, after touching it, to count as a rejection.

settings.label: Break displacement (daily ATR)
settings.html: A close this far through a zone breaks it at once.

settings.label: Closes beyond zone for break
settings.html: Consecutive closes beyond a zone that also break it.

settings.label: Closes in / through zone for acceptance
settings.html: Consecutive closes inside a zone before it is marked accepting.

settings.label: Event-state hold bars
settings.html: How long a rejecting, accepting or flipped state is kept once price has left the zone.

settings.label: Broken-zone flip watch (minutes)
settings.html: How long a broken zone is watched for a retest from the other side.

settings.label: Flip retest tolerance (daily ATR)
settings.html: How close to a broken zone price must come to count as a retest.

settings.label: Previous day / close
settings.html: Use the previous session's high, low and close as candidate levels.

settings.label: Previous week
settings.html: Use the previous week's regular-session high and low as candidate levels.

settings.label: Premarket high / low
settings.html: Use today's premarket high and low as candidate levels.

settings.label: Finalized opening range
settings.html: Use the high and low of the finished opening range as candidate levels.

settings.label: RTH open
settings.html: Use the regular-session open as a candidate level.

settings.label: Confirmed swing pivots
settings.html: Use confirmed swing highs and lows as candidate levels.

settings.label: Pivot left bars
settings.html: Bars on the left a swing high or low must stand above or below.

settings.label: Pivot right bars
settings.html: Bars on the right needed to confirm a swing, which is also how late it is known.

settings.label: Maximum pivot records
settings.html: How many swing levels are kept; the oldest goes first.

settings.label: Pivot maximum age (bars)
settings.html: Swing levels older than this many bars are dropped.

settings.label: Pivot recency decay (bars)
settings.html: Sets how fast a level's recency score fades with the age of its swing or last touch.

settings.label: Adaptive round numbers
settings.html: Use the round numbers just below and above the close, with a step that grows with price.

settings.label: ATR projections
settings.html: Add levels half and one daily ATR from the session open, and one daily ATR from the previous close.

settings.label: Gap structure
settings.html: Track an opening gap and use its midpoint and unfilled edge as candidate levels until it fills.

settings.label: Minimum gap (daily ATR)
settings.html: The smallest gap from the previous close to the open that counts, in daily ATR.

settings.label: RTH VWAP as candidate
settings.html: Use the regular-session VWAP as a candidate level during the session.

settings.label: VWAP bands as candidates
settings.html: Also use the first VWAP deviation bands as candidate levels.

settings.label: Reaction lookback bars
settings.html: How many bars back the touches of a level are searched.

settings.label: Reaction observation bars
settings.html: How many bars after a touch are measured to score the reaction.

settings.label: Touch cooldown bars
settings.html: Touches closer together than this count as one.

settings.label: Maximum historical touches scored
settings.html: The most recent touches of a level that are scored.

settings.label: Touch tolerance (ticks)
settings.html: The smallest distance, in ticks, at which a bar counts as touching a level.

settings.label: Touch tolerance (daily ATR)
settings.html: The touch distance as a fraction of the daily ATR, used when it is wider than the tick minimum.

settings.label: Event AVWAP anchor
settings.html: How the event VWAP is anchored: the automatic mode has no event calendar and never anchors, Manual timestamp anchors at the time you enter, and Disabled turns it off.

settings.label: Manual event timestamp
settings.html: The event time as YYYY-MM-DD or YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM in the session timezone; outside the session it anchors at the next open.

settings.label: Maximum event age (days)
settings.html: The event VWAP stops counting as a level after this many days.

settings.label: Minimum bars before AVWAP contributes
settings.html: Bars the event VWAP must cover before it becomes a candidate level.

settings.label: Maximum AVWAP distance (daily ATR)
settings.html: The event VWAP is used only while it is within this many daily ATRs of the close.

settings.label: Show regular-session VWAP
settings.html: Plot the VWAP of the regular session during session hours.

settings.label: VWAP source
settings.html: The price averaged by the session VWAP and its bands.

settings.label: Show +/-1 stdev band
settings.html: Plot the first pair of volume-weighted deviation bands around the VWAP.

settings.label: Show +/-2 stdev band
settings.html: Plot the second pair of volume-weighted deviation bands around the VWAP.

settings.label: Band 1 multiplier
settings.html: Volume-weighted standard deviations from the VWAP to the first band.

settings.label: Band 2 multiplier
settings.html: Volume-weighted standard deviations from the VWAP to the second band.

settings.label: Show 9 / 21 EMA in Legacy / Debug
settings.html: Plot the 9 and 21 bar exponential averages of the close when the display mode is Legacy / Debug.

settings.label: Enable transition alerts
settings.html: Raise alerts when price enters, rejects, accepts or breaks a zone, when a zone flips, and when a stronger zone is chosen.

settings.label: Show research values in the dashboard
settings.html: Add the zone prices, strengths, actionability, nearest state and gap levels as extra dashboard rows.

faq.q: Why do I only see the VWAP line and a few boxes?
faq.html: The default display mode, Reaction Zones, draws the two zones, their edge bands and the opening-range box. Switch the display mode to Zones + Key References to plot the previous day, week, premarket, opening range and session open lines as well.

faq.q: What is the difference between strength and actionability?
faq.html: Strength rates the cluster itself from the scores and variety of its levels. Actionability is that strength discounted by how far the zone sits from the close, so a strong zone a long way off can rank below a slightly weaker one next to price.

faq.q: Which session times should I use?
faq.html: Set the timezone and the regular and premarket windows to the hours of the instrument you trade, for example Asia/Kolkata with a 0915-1530 regular session for Indian equities. The previous day, opening range, gap and session VWAP all follow these windows.

faq.q: Does the automatic event anchor do anything?
faq.html: No. There is no event calendar to read, so the automatic mode never anchors. Choose Manual timestamp and enter a date and time to anchor the event VWAP yourself.

options-levels.deviation: A timezone that OpenScript does not recognise, such as an abbreviation like EST or a misspelt name, stops the study with an unknown-timezone error instead of falling back to another zone, because this version of OpenScript cannot test a zone name before using it.

momentum-investing-setup-with-scanner.title: Momentum Investing Setup with Scanner
momentum-investing-setup-with-scanner.summary: Flags a bar only when the 250-bar change, RSI, MFI, CCI and a volume surge all agree, with Supertrend on price and mini oscillator curves under the candles.
momentum-investing-setup-with-scanner.descriptionHtml:
This setup is a five-filter momentum screen drawn on the price chart. A bar is flagged Long only when all five agree on strength: the percentage change from the close 250 bars back is above the threshold, RSI is above its overbought level, the Money Flow Index is above its overbought level, CCI is above its overbought level, and the bar's volume is larger than its exponential average multiplied by the volume multiplier. A Short needs the mirror image on every filter: the change below the negative threshold and each oscillator below its oversold level, again on a volume surge.

The percentage change is measured as the move over 250 bars divided by the current close. RSI is computed on the close, MFI on the typical price (high, low and close averaged) with volume, and CCI on the typical price. The volume average is an exponential average seeded with the simple average of its first values. A Supertrend line rides the price, drawn in green while the trend is up and in red while it is down, with the line breaking at each flip.

Over the most recent bars, set by Display Length, the study redraws RSI with its simple average, MFI, and CCI with its simple average as small curves in price space below the candles, each with its overbought, middle and oversold levels and a tag showing the latest reading. A volume histogram sits above the candles with the volume threshold (the average times the multiplier) running through it, and a tag giving the buying and selling share of the newest bar, its volume and that threshold. The histogram is drawn only when the newest bar carries volume. A small table in a corner lists the latest value of each filter, coloured green, red or grey by its verdict.
momentum-investing-setup-with-scanner.howToReadHtml:
A Long triangle under a bar, with the candle recoloured light green, means price, momentum, money flow and volume all pointed up on that bar. A Short triangle above a bar, with a light red candle, is the same agreement to the downside. Signal bars near the newest bar, within roughly Display Length bars, are also shaded. The Supertrend line gives a trailing level to judge whether the move is holding.

The table shows which filters are already in place and which are missing, which is useful between signals. The volume filter is strict by design: with the multiplier at 5 a bar needs five times its average volume, so signals are rare and a chart can show none for a long stretch. The 250-bar change also means nothing can be flagged until 250 bars of history exist. The mini curves are rescaled to the recent price range, so read them for shape and position against their own levels, not for their price.

settings.label: Above/Below %
settings.html: The 250-bar percentage change a bar must exceed for a long signal, or fall below the negative of for a short signal. Lower it on intraday charts.

settings.label: RSI Display
settings.html: Draw the RSI curve, its average, its levels and its tag below the candles. The RSI filter still applies when this is off.

settings.label: RSI Length
settings.html: Bars in the RSI calculation. A longer length gives a smoother, slower reading.

settings.label: RSI SMA Length
settings.html: Bars in the simple average drawn with the RSI curve. It does not affect the signals.

settings.label: RSI Overbought
settings.html: The RSI level a long signal must be above, also drawn as the upper reference line.

settings.label: RSI Oversold
settings.html: The RSI level a short signal must be below, also drawn as the lower reference line.

settings.label: RSI Vertical Offset
settings.html: How far below the recent low the RSI curve sits, in multiples of the recent price range. Larger moves it further down.

settings.label: RSI Height
settings.html: How tall the RSI curve is drawn, as a multiple of the recent price range.

settings.label: MFI Display
settings.html: Draw the Money Flow Index curve, its levels and its tag below the candles. The MFI filter still applies when this is off.

settings.label: MFI Length
settings.html: Bars in the Money Flow Index window.

settings.label: MFI Overbought
settings.html: The MFI level a long signal must be above, also drawn as the upper reference line.

settings.label: MFI Oversold
settings.html: The MFI level a short signal must be below, also drawn as the lower reference line.

settings.label: MFI Vertical Offset
settings.html: How far below the recent low the MFI curve sits, in multiples of the recent price range.

settings.label: MFI Height
settings.html: How tall the MFI curve is drawn, as a multiple of the recent price range.

settings.label: CCI Display
settings.html: Draw the CCI curve, its average, its levels and its tag below the candles. The CCI filter still applies when this is off.

settings.label: CCI Length
settings.html: Bars in the Commodity Channel Index calculation on the typical price.

settings.label: CCI SMA Length
settings.html: Bars in the simple average drawn with the CCI curve. It does not affect the signals.

settings.label: CCI Overbought
settings.html: The CCI level a long signal must be above, also drawn as the upper reference line.

settings.label: CCI Oversold
settings.html: The CCI level a short signal must be below, also drawn as the lower reference line.

settings.label: CCI Vertical Offset
settings.html: How far below the recent low the CCI curve sits, in multiples of the recent price range.

settings.label: CCI Height
settings.html: How tall the CCI curve is drawn. CCI runs on a wider scale than RSI and MFI, so this is kept small.

settings.label: Display MA Line
settings.html: Draw the volume threshold (the exponential average times the multiplier) as a line through the volume histogram.

settings.label: Type
settings.html: Regular Volume colours each histogram bar by the candle direction; Buying/Selling Volume draws the whole bar in green with the selling share over it in red; None hides the histogram, its threshold line and its tag.

settings.label: MA Length
settings.html: Bars in the exponential volume average that the volume filter compares against.

settings.label: MA Multiplier (x)
settings.html: How many times its average the volume must be for a signal. 1 means any above-average bar qualifies; 5 asks for a strong surge.

settings.label: Volume Vertical Offset
settings.html: How far above the recent high the volume histogram starts, in multiples of the recent price range.

settings.label: Volume Height
settings.html: How tall the tallest histogram bar is drawn, as a multiple of the recent price range.

settings.label: Supertrend Display
settings.html: Show or hide the Supertrend line. The line plays no part in the signals.

settings.label: ATR Length
settings.html: Bars in the average true range that sets the Supertrend's distance from price.

settings.label: Factor
settings.html: Multiple of the average true range between price and the Supertrend line. Larger values flip less often.

settings.label: Display Length
settings.html: How many recent bars the mini curves and the volume histogram cover, and roughly how far back signal bars are shaded. The shading counts bar intervals back from the chart clock, so on a market with session breaks it covers fewer bars.

settings.label: Position
settings.html: Where the readout table sits. A table here can only sit in a corner: Top Left and Middle Left go to the top left, Bottom Left to the bottom left, Bottom Center and Bottom Right to the bottom right, and the other three to the top right.

settings.label: Size
settings.html: Kept with the other table settings, but a table here has no text size, so it does not change the drawing.

faq.q: Why are there no signals on my chart?
faq.html: All five filters must agree on the same bar, and the volume filter asks for five times the average volume by default. That is rare on most instruments. Lower MA Multiplier (x) or the percentage threshold to see more signals, and remember that nothing can fire until 250 bars of history exist.

faq.q: What do the curves below the candles show?
faq.html: They are RSI, MFI and CCI redrawn in price space over the most recent bars, each with its overbought, middle and oversold lines. Their height is scaled to the recent price range, so the price axis does not read their values; the tag beside each curve gives the latest reading.

faq.q: Does the Supertrend line affect the signals?
faq.html: No. The signals come only from the five filters. Supertrend is drawn as a trailing level to judge whether a move is holding after a signal.

faq.q: Is the percentage change measured from the old close?
faq.html: No. The move over 250 bars is divided by the current close, not the close 250 bars back, so the figure is a little smaller than a plain rate of change after a large rise.

momentum-investing-setup-with-scanner.deviation: Signal bars are shaded by counting whole chart intervals back from the chart clock rather than by counting bars, because a study cannot know on an earlier bar how many bars follow it, so on a market that closes, or when the clock is well past the newest bar, fewer bars are shaded; and the readout table sits in the nearest of four corners at the chart text size, because a table here has no centre positions and no size setting.

faq.q: Why are there no signals on my chart?
faq.html: All five filters must agree on the same bar, and the volume filter asks for five times the average volume by default. That is rare on most instruments. Lower MA Multiplier (x) or the percentage threshold to see more signals, and remember that nothing can fire on the first 250 bars of a chart.

faq.q: What do the curves below the candles show?
faq.html: They are MFI, RSI and CCI redrawn in price space over the most recent bars, each with its overbought, middle and oversold lines. Their height is scaled to the recent price range, so the price axis does not read their values; the caption beside each panel gives the latest reading.

faq.q: Does the Supertrend line affect the signals?
faq.html: No. The signals come only from the five filters. Supertrend is drawn as a trailing level to judge whether a move is holding after a signal.

faq.q: Is the percentage change measured from the old close?
faq.html: No. The move over 250 bars is divided by the current close, not the close 250 bars back, so after a rise the figure is smaller than a plain rate of change and after a fall it is larger in size: a close that has doubled reads 50%, not 100%.

momentum-investing-setup.deviation: Signal bars are shaded by counting whole chart intervals back from the chart clock rather than by counting bars, because a study cannot know on an earlier bar how many bars follow it, so on a market that closes, or when the clock is well past the newest bar, fewer bars are shaded; and the readout table sits in the nearest of four corners at the chart's own text size, because a table here has no centre positions and no size setting.

rsi-directional-momentum-scanner.title: RSI Directional Momentum Scanner
rsi-directional-momentum-scanner.summary: An RSI setup scanner: RSI crosses 60 or 40, pulls back, then price breaks the setup candle, with retracement, flip and divergence modes.
rsi-directional-momentum-scanner.descriptionHtml:
The scanner runs a small state machine on an RSI (14 bars by default) and a simple average of that RSI (also 14 bars by default). A long setup starts when RSI crosses above 60 while it is above its average; that candle's high becomes the break level. RSI then has to dip back below 60, and the setup completes on the first settled bar that closes above the break level while RSI is again above 60 and above its average. A short setup is the mirror image around 40, using the low of the crossing candle. A new crossing on the other side cancels a setup that is still waiting.

The six scanning methods read that machine in different ways. Continuous Break marks the crossing candle (a circle) and the break (a triangle marked 2). Continuous Retracement also marks the first bar from the break onward whose high (for a short) or low (for a long) crosses back through a Fibonacci level of the breaking candle, set by Fib Value (marked 3). Flip Break and Flip Retracement keep only the breaks or retracements that change side from the previous one. Divergence and Hidden Divergence ignore the machine and join RSI pivots with a line in the RSI pane when price and RSI disagree: a lower price low with a higher RSI low is bullish, a higher price high with a lower RSI high is bearish, and the hidden forms are the reverse pairs.

Optional filters can veto the break bar: the day's running percentage change, the day's cumulative volume or its change against the previous day, the candle's range against the average true range or against the previous candle's range, the share of the range taken by the body, the bar's volume against its average, relative volume, a clock window and a single calendar date. Days are calendar days in the chart's timezone. A small table on the newest bar shows the day's running percentage change (the sum of the bar-to-bar percentage changes of the close since the day began), today's volume so far against the previous day's total in percent, and both days' volume in lakhs (units of 100,000).
rsi-directional-momentum-scanner.howToReadHtml:
In the RSI pane, the blue line is RSI and the orange line its average, with the 60 to 40 band shaded and dotted lines at 70, 50 and 30. On the bars, a circle is a fresh crossing that starts a setup, a triangle marked 2 is a completed break and a triangle marked 3 is the retracement entry; marks above the bar and a red tint are short, marks below and a green tint are long. Breaks and retracements also shade the background, and every marked bar is recoloured.

The Signal Level line on the price chart shows the break level from the setup candle to the break, or the Fibonacci level from the break to the retracement. It is drawn 80 bars behind the newest bar, because a span is only known once its setup completes, so the newest setups show their marks long before their level line. A break is only taken on a settled bar, and none of the marks is a forecast; treat them as candidates to study, not as instructions.

settings.label: Scanning Method
settings.html: Which signals the scanner marks: the break, the retracement, only side flips of either, or classic or hidden RSI divergence.

settings.label: Long Signals
settings.html: Show the long marks, bar colours and background shading. Turning it off hides them without changing the calculation.

settings.label: Short Signals
settings.html: Show the short marks, bar colours and background shading. Turning it off hides them without changing the calculation.

settings.label: RSI Length
settings.html: The number of bars in the RSI. Longer settings cross 60 and 40 less often, so setups are fewer and slower.

settings.label: RSI Source
settings.html: The price series the RSI is computed from, close by default.

settings.label: SMA Length
settings.html: The length of the simple average of RSI that a setup and its break must sit on the right side of.

settings.label: Fib Value
settings.html: Where in the breaking candle the retracement level sits: 0 is the low of a long breaking candle and the high of a short one, 1 the opposite edge and 0.5 the midpoint.

settings.label: Display Bullish Divergence
settings.html: In Divergence mode, draw the lines for a lower price low with a higher RSI low.

settings.label: Display Bearish Divergence
settings.html: In Divergence mode, draw the lines for a higher price high with a lower RSI high.

settings.label: Display Hidden Bullish Divergence
settings.html: In Hidden Divergence mode, draw the lines for a higher price low with a lower RSI low.

settings.label: Display Hidden Bearish Divergence
settings.html: In Hidden Divergence mode, draw the lines for a lower price high with a higher RSI high.

settings.label: Pivot Lookback Right
settings.html: Bars after an RSI pivot that must confirm it. A pivot, and any divergence line ending at it, appears this many bars late.

settings.label: Pivot Lookback Left
settings.html: Bars before an RSI pivot that must sit above a low pivot or below a high pivot.

settings.label: Max of Lookback Range
settings.html: The most bars allowed between the previous pivot and the current one for the pair to count as a divergence.

settings.label: Min of Lookback Range
settings.html: The fewest bars allowed between the previous pivot and the current one for the pair to count as a divergence.

settings.label: Apply % Change Filter
settings.html: Requires the day's change to be above the figure below and below its negative at once, so turning it on stops every break and retracement.

settings.label: % Change Above/Below +/-
settings.html: The day percentage change threshold used by the change filter, in both directions.

settings.label: Apply Volume Filter
settings.html: Allow a break only when the volume traded so far today is at least the figure below.

settings.label: Volume Above
settings.html: The cumulative day volume the volume filter requires, in units of the instrument.

settings.label: Apply Volume % Change Filter
settings.html: Allow a break only when today's volume so far has grown by at least the figure below against the previous day's total.

settings.label: Volume % Change Above
settings.html: The volume growth in percent the volume change filter requires. 0 means today must already exceed the previous day.

settings.label: Apply ATR Filter
settings.html: Allow a break only on a candle whose range is larger than the average true range times the multiplier.

settings.label: ATR Length
settings.html: The number of bars in the average true range used by the ATR filter.

settings.label: ATR Multiplier
settings.html: How many average true ranges the breaking candle's range must exceed when the ATR filter is on.

settings.label: Apply Body % Filter
settings.html: Allow a break only on a candle whose body covers at least the stated share of its range.

settings.label: Body % Above
settings.html: The share of the candle's range, in percent, that the body must cover for the body filters.

settings.label: Apply Body Size Filter
settings.html: Allow a break only on a candle that passes the body share test and whose range is at least the multiplier times the previous candle's range.

settings.label: Body Size Multiplier (x)
settings.html: How many times the previous candle's range the breaking candle must span when the body size filter is on.

settings.label: Apply Volume SMA Filter
settings.html: Allow a break only on a bar whose volume is above the simple average of volume.

settings.label: Volume SMA Length
settings.html: The number of bars in the volume average used by the volume average filter.

settings.label: Apply Relative Volume Filter
settings.html: Allow a break only when relative volume, this bar's volume over the previous bar's volume average, is above its own average times the multiplier.

settings.label: Relative Volume Length
settings.html: The length of the volume average and of the relative volume average used by the relative volume filter.

settings.label: Rel Vol SMA Multiplier
settings.html: How many times its own average the relative volume must reach when the relative volume filter is on.

settings.label: Apply Time Filter
settings.html: Allow a break only between the From and To times below, read on the chart's clock. The To time itself is excluded.

settings.label: Time From (hour)
settings.html: The hour the time window opens, 0 to 23, on the chart's clock.

settings.label: Time From (minute)
settings.html: The minute the time window opens, added to the From hour.

settings.label: Time To (hour)
settings.html: The hour the time window closes, 0 to 23, on the chart's clock.

settings.label: Time To (minute)
settings.html: The minute the time window closes, added to the To hour.

settings.label: Apply Date Filter
settings.html: Allow a break only on the single calendar date set below, in the chart's timezone.

settings.label: Day
settings.html: The day of the month the date filter accepts.

settings.label: Month
settings.html: The month, 1 to 12, the date filter accepts.

settings.label: Year
settings.html: The year the date filter accepts.

settings.label: Display
settings.html: Show the table of the day's change and volume on the newest bar.

settings.label: Position
settings.html: Where the table sits. The grid can only pin to a corner, so the left positions use a left corner, the others a right corner, and the middle row uses the top corners.

faq.q: Why does a setup sometimes never complete?
faq.html: A setup waits until price closes beyond the crossing candle while RSI is back on the right side of 60 or 40 and of its average. If RSI crosses the opposite band first, the waiting setup is replaced by one on the other side, and nothing is marked for the old one.

faq.q: Why is the Signal Level line missing on the newest bars?
faq.html: The line covers the bars from a setup candle to its break, which are only known once the break happens. The study fills the line in 80 bars later and draws it back over the bars it describes, so the newest 80 bars show the marks and colours but not the line.

faq.q: What does the Flip method add over the Continuous methods?
faq.html: Flip Break marks a break only when it is on the opposite side from the previous break, and Flip Retracement does the same for retracements. A run of breaks on one side gives one mark instead of many, and the very first break on the chart is never marked.

faq.q: Why does turning on the % Change Filter stop every break?
faq.html: The filter asks for the day's running change to be above the threshold and below its negative on the same bar, which cannot happen, so no break, retracement or flip is ever marked. The circles that start a setup do not pass through the filters, so they still appear in the two Continuous modes.

rsi-directional-momentum-scanner.deviation: The Signal Level line is filled in 80 bars late and drawn back over the bars it covers, so the newest 80 bars never show it and a span longer than 81 bars shows only its last 81 bars, because a study cannot repaint earlier bars once a setup completes.
rsi-directional-momentum-scanner.credit: Original work (c) Arun K Bhaskar, MPL-2.0

rsi-directional-momentum.title: RSI Directional Momentum
rsi-directional-momentum.summary: An RSI pane with a three-step breakout scanner on top: RSI breaks 60 or 40, pulls back, then price clears the breaking candle, plus retracement, flip and divergence modes.
rsi-directional-momentum.descriptionHtml:
The study draws a standard RSI with a simple moving average of the RSI, a shaded band between 60 and 40, and dotted reference levels at 70, 50 and 30. On top of that pane it runs a scanner that looks for one of six setups, chosen with the Scanning Method menu.

Continuous Break is a three-step state machine. On the short side, step one is RSI crossing below 40 while it is under its own average; the low of that breaking candle is remembered. Step two is RSI climbing back above 40. Step three is a confirmed bar that closes below the remembered low while RSI is again below 40 and below its average, and while every enabled filter passes. The long side is the mirror image around 60 and the high of the breaking candle. A guide line on the price chart runs from the breaking candle to the signal bar at the level that was broken. Continuous Retracement goes one step further: after a signal it waits for price to cross back into the signal candle at the Fib Value fraction of its range, and draws that level as a guide. Flip Break and Flip Retracement report only the signals that change side, so a run of shorts shows once.

Divergence and Hidden Divergence use RSI pivots found with the left and right lookbacks. A regular bullish divergence is a lower price low with a higher RSI low; a hidden bullish divergence is a higher price low with a lower RSI low, and the bearish cases mirror them on pivot highs. The previous pivot must sit between the minimum and maximum lookback range. Every pivot is plotted on the RSI pane and on price, and only the pivots that complete the chosen divergence are coloured; the others are drawn fully transparent. A small table in the corner shows the running day's percentage change, its volume, the change in volume against the previous day, and the previous day's volume, with both volumes shown in lakhs (units of 100,000).
rsi-directional-momentum.howToReadHtml:
In the continuous modes a circle above the bar marks a short step one and a circle below marks a long step one; a triangle marked 2 is the completed break and a triangle marked 3 is the retracement entry. The numbered bars are also recoloured and lightly shaded; a step one bar is recoloured but not shaded. Treat step one as a warning that momentum has turned, and the numbered marks as the setup the scanner exists to find. The divergence modes add no markers: read the coloured pivot points on the RSI pane and on price.

The marks are mechanical. They do not judge trend, support or news, and a break can fail on the next bar. The extra filters (day change, volume, ATR, body size, relative volume, time and date) only remove signals; the day change filter as written needs the day to be above +N and below -N at once, so switching it on removes every signal. Because the guide levels are only known once a sequence completes, they appear on the chart 120 bars after the bar they belong to, so the newest stretch of the chart shows the markers but not yet their guides.

settings.label: Scanning Method
settings.html: Which setup the scanner looks for: the continuous break, its retracement, the two flip versions that report only changes of side, or regular or hidden RSI divergence.

settings.label: Long Signals
settings.html: Show the long side markers, bar colours and shading of the scanner.

settings.label: Short Signals
settings.html: Show the short side markers, bar colours and shading of the scanner.

settings.label: RSI Length
settings.html: Number of bars in the RSI. A shorter length makes RSI cross 60 and 40 more often, so the scanner finds more sequences.

settings.label: RSI Source
settings.html: The price series the RSI is computed from, the close by default.

settings.label: SMA Length
settings.html: Length of the simple average of the RSI that each step compares RSI against.

settings.label: Fib Value
settings.html: Where in the signal candle the retracement level sits: 0 is the low of a long signal candle and the high of a short one, 1 the other end, 0.5 the midpoint.

settings.label: Display Bullish Divergence
settings.html: In Divergence mode, colour the legs where price made a lower low and RSI a higher low.

settings.label: Display Bearish Divergence
settings.html: In Divergence mode, colour the legs where price made a higher high and RSI a lower high.

settings.label: Display Hidden Bullish Divergence
settings.html: In Hidden Divergence mode, colour the legs where price made a higher low and RSI a lower low.

settings.label: Display Hidden Bearish Divergence
settings.html: In Hidden Divergence mode, colour the legs where price made a lower high and RSI a higher high.

settings.label: Pivot Lookback Right
settings.html: Bars after an RSI pivot that must stay above (or below) it. A pivot is confirmed this many bars late. Points are drawn on their pivot for values up to 5, though below 5 the newest point appears 5 bars after its pivot rather than this many; above 5 each point lands that many bars minus 5 after its pivot.

settings.label: Pivot Lookback Left
settings.html: Bars before an RSI pivot that must stay above (or below) it. Larger values find fewer, more significant pivots.

settings.label: Max of Lookback Range
settings.html: The furthest back, in bars, the previous pivot may be for a divergence to count.

settings.label: Min of Lookback Range
settings.html: The nearest, in bars, the previous pivot may be for a divergence to count.

settings.label: Apply % Change Filter
settings.html: Require the running day's percentage change to be above +N and below -N. Both at once cannot hold, so switching this on blocks every completed signal.

settings.label: % Change Above/Below +/-
settings.html: The N, in percent, for the day change filter.

settings.label: Apply Volume Filter (Day Total)
settings.html: Require the running day's total volume to reach the level set below before a signal completes.

settings.label: Volume Above
settings.html: The day total volume the volume filter asks for.

settings.label: Apply Volume % Change Filter
settings.html: Require the running day's volume to be up on the previous day's total by at least the percentage below.

settings.label: Volume % Change Above
settings.html: The volume change, in percent against the previous day, that the filter asks for. 0 means simply more than the previous day.

settings.label: Apply ATR Filter
settings.html: Require the signal candle's range to exceed the ATR times the multiplier, which keeps only wide candles.

settings.label: ATR Length
settings.html: Number of bars in the average true range used by the ATR filter.

settings.label: ATR Multiplier
settings.html: How many ATRs the signal candle's range must exceed when the ATR filter is on.

settings.label: Apply Body % Filter
settings.html: Require the candle body to cover at least the set share of the candle's full range.

settings.label: Body % Above
settings.html: The share of the range, in percent, the body must cover. It is also used by the body size filter.

settings.label: Apply Body Size Filter
settings.html: Require a full-bodied candle whose range is at least the multiplier times the previous candle's range.

settings.label: Body Size Multiplier (x)
settings.html: How many times larger than the previous candle the signal candle must be for the body size filter.

settings.label: Apply Volume Filter (vs SMA)
settings.html: Require the signal candle's volume to be above its simple moving average.

settings.label: Volume SMA Length
settings.html: Number of bars in the volume average used by that filter.

settings.label: Apply Relative Volume Filter
settings.html: Require relative volume (volume over the previous bar's average volume) to exceed its own average times the multiplier.

settings.label: Relative Volume Length
settings.html: Number of bars in both averages behind the relative volume filter.

settings.label: Rel Vol SMA Multiplier
settings.html: How far relative volume must stand above its own average for the filter to pass.

settings.label: Apply Time Filter
settings.html: Allow signals only between the start and end times below, read in the chart's time zone.

settings.label: Time From (Hour)
settings.html: Hour at which the time window opens.

settings.label: Time From (Minute)
settings.html: Minute at which the time window opens.

settings.label: Time To (Hour)
settings.html: Hour at which the time window closes; a bar at the closing minute is outside it.

settings.label: Time To (Minute)
settings.html: Minute at which the time window closes.

settings.label: Apply Date Filter
settings.html: Allow signals only on the one calendar date set below, useful for studying a single session.

settings.label: Day
settings.html: Day of the month for the date filter.

settings.label: Month
settings.html: Month, 1 to 12, for the date filter.

settings.label: Year
settings.html: Year for the date filter.

settings.label: Display
settings.html: Show the table of the day's percentage change and volume readings.

settings.label: Position
settings.html: Kept with the other table settings; the table is always drawn in the bottom right corner of the pane in this version.

settings.label: Size
settings.html: Kept with the other table settings; the table is drawn at the chart's standard text size in this version.

faq.q: Why do the break and retracement guide lines appear late?
faq.html: A guide runs back to the candle that started the sequence, and that is only known once the sequence completes. A plot cannot go back and fill bars it has already drawn, so the study holds each guide for 120 bars and then draws it on the bars it belongs to. The markers and bar colours are not delayed.

faq.q: What do the numbers 2 and 3 on the markers mean?
faq.html: 2 marks the completed break, the third step of the sequence, where the close cleared the breaking candle. 3 marks the retracement, where price came back to the Fib Value level of that signal candle. The plain circles mark step one, the RSI break itself.

faq.q: Why does turning on the % change filter remove every signal?
faq.html: The rule asks for the day's change to be above +N and below -N at the same time, which cannot happen. It is kept as written so the study computes the same thing as its rules state.

faq.q: Why are most divergence points invisible?
faq.html: Every RSI pivot is plotted, but a point is coloured only when it completes the divergence the selected mode looks for, measured against the previous pivot inside the lookback range. The rest are drawn fully transparent.

rsi-directional-momentum.deviation: The break and retracement guide levels are drawn 120 bars after the bar they belong to, because a plot cannot write onto bars already drawn, so the newest 120 bars show no guide yet and a sequence longer than 120 bars loses its oldest part; with a Pivot Lookback Right above 5 each divergence point lands that many bars minus 5 after its pivot, because a plot's offset cannot be computed from a setting; the guides and the 60 and 40 band lines are solid, because a plot has no dotted style; and the table always sits bottom right at the standard text size, because a table offers only four corners and no text size.
rsi-directional-momentum.credit: Original work (c) Arun K Bhaskar, MPL-2.0

option-buying-scalping-setup-scanner.title: Option Buying Scalping Setup Scanner
option-buying-scalping-setup-scanner.summary: A directional scalping setup that marks long and short bars when Supertrend, an anchored VWAP, MACD and Stochastic all agree, with optional candle, volume and time filters.
option-buying-scalping-setup-scanner.descriptionHtml:
This study stacks several familiar tools on the price chart and only marks a bar when they all point the same way. It draws four exponential moving averages (20, 50, 100 and 200 by default, each seeded with the simple mean of its first window), a VWAP or TWAP that restarts at the start of each anchor period (one day by default), and a Supertrend built from a 10-bar average true range at a factor of 3. MACD (3, 9, 15) and a Stochastic (5, 3, 3) are computed alongside and redrawn as small scaled panels inside the price pane over the most recent bars, together with a volume panel.

A long entry needs the close above the Supertrend and above the VWAP, %K above the oversold level and above %D, and the MACD line above zero, above its signal line and above its histogram. A short entry is the mirror image, with %K below the overbought level. Every enabled filter must also pass: a bar range larger than a multiple of ATR, a body that fills a set share of the bar, a body that passes that test on a bar whose range is at least a set multiple of the previous bar's range, volume above its average, relative volume above its multiplied average, and a clock window.

Two signal methods decide which entry bars are marked. Continuous Signals arms when MACD sits on the opposite side of zero and fires on the first full entry after that, then disarms. Flip Signals marks only the bar where the entry state changes from long to short or back.
option-buying-scalping-setup-scanner.howToReadHtml:
A small triangle below a candle is a long signal and one above is a short signal; the candle itself is recoloured on that bar, and the background is shaded on signal bars among the most recent bars. Read the Supertrend colour and the side of the VWAP as the trend filter, and the mini panels as a quick look at momentum and volume without opening separate panes.

The panels are scaled into the price range of the recent bars, so their height means nothing in price terms: only their shape and crossings matter. Signals need every condition on the same bar, so they are deliberately rare, and in a choppy market they can still fire on both sides in quick succession. The study reads only the chart's own symbol; it does not scan a list of other symbols. Treat a mark as a setup to check, not as an order.

faq.q: Why do I see fewer signals with Continuous Signals than I expect?
faq.html: In that mode a long signal first needs the MACD line below zero to arm, and fires on the first bar after that where every long condition holds. After it fires it disarms, so the next long signal needs MACD to dip below zero again.

faq.q: What do the small panels inside the price chart show?
faq.html: They are MACD, Stochastic and volume, rescaled into the price range of the most recent bars so they fit in the same pane. Their vertical position and height are set by the offset and height settings and carry no price meaning.

faq.q: Do the moving averages affect the signals?
faq.html: No. The four exponential averages are drawn for context only. The signals use the Supertrend, the VWAP or TWAP, MACD, the Stochastic and any filters you switch on.

faq.q: Which clock does the time filter use?
faq.html: The bar's opening time in the chart's timezone. A bar is kept when it starts at or after the From time and before the To time.

option-buying-scalping-setup-scanner.deviation: The background shading is meant to cover signal bars among the newest Display Length bars, but a study cannot know in advance which bar will be the newest, so it counts whole chart intervals back from the chart's clock: on a market that closes, or when the clock is well past the newest bar, fewer bars are shaded, and where the chart supplies no clock none are.

option-buying-scalping-setup.title: Option Buying Scalping Setup
option-buying-scalping-setup.summary: A directional scalping setup that marks the bar where VWAP, Supertrend, MACD and Stochastic all agree on one side after a MACD pullback.
option-buying-scalping-setup.descriptionHtml:
This setup looks for a short, sharp move in the direction several tools already agree on. On the chart it draws four exponential moving averages (20, 50, 100 and 200 by default), a VWAP that restarts at the start of each anchor period (or a TWAP, the plain average of ohlc4 since the anchor, for symbols without volume), and a Supertrend line that is green while the trend is up and red while it is down.

A long signal needs every one of these at once: the close above the Supertrend and above the VWAP, the Stochastic %K above the Over Sold level and above its %D, and a fast MACD (3, 9, 15 by default) that is positive and above both its signal line and its histogram. A short signal is the mirror image. In Continuous mode the signal is armed only after the MACD has been on the other side of zero, so it fires on the first bar that completes the setup after a pullback, then re-arms. In Flip mode a signal appears only on the bar where the qualifying side changes from long to short or back.

Optional filters can drop signal bars that are too small against the ATR, have too small a body, are not larger than the previous bar, or carry too little volume or relative volume, and a time filter keeps only bars inside a clock window. On the newest bar the study also draws small Stochastic, MACD and volume panels over the price pane, scaled into bands below and above the recent price range.
option-buying-scalping-setup.howToReadHtml:
A pale red triangle above a bar and a pale red candle mark a short setup; a pale green triangle below a bar and a pale green candle mark a long one. Signal bars near the right edge also get a faint shade in the same colour, while the candle colour and the triangles cover the whole chart. Read a long signal as a pullback that has turned back in the direction the Supertrend, the VWAP, the Stochastic and the MACD all agree on. The four averages are drawn for context only and play no part in the signal.

The miniature panels are a quick glance at momentum and participation without opening extra panes: the Stochastic with its three levels at the bottom, the MACD with a coloured histogram below the price range, and volume bars with their average above it. They are redrawn on every new bar and are not a separate oscillator scale. The setup has many conditions, so it fires rarely on quiet charts and can lag a fast reversal. It describes past bars and does not predict the next one.

faq.q: Why does a signal sometimes not appear even though the trend looks clear?
faq.html: In Continuous mode the MACD first has to be on the other side of zero to arm the setup. A trend that never pulls back far enough for that does not fire again until it does.

faq.q: What is the difference between Continuous and Flip?
faq.html: Continuous marks every completed pullback setup while the side holds, so it can mark several bars in one trend. Flip marks only the bar where the qualifying side changes, and the very first side the chart ever takes is not marked because there is nothing before it to change from.

faq.q: Why are the MACD and Stochastic drawn over the price chart?
faq.html: They are compact panels scaled into bands just below the recent price range, with volume above it, so momentum and participation can be read without extra panes. Only their shape matters, not the price level they sit at.

faq.q: Should I use VWAP or TWAP?
faq.html: Use VWAP when the symbol has volume. A missing volume leaves VWAP blank until the next anchor, and then no signal can fire, so choose TWAP for an index or any symbol without volume.

sideways-market-skipper-scanner.title: Sideways Market Skipper Scanner
sideways-market-skipper-scanner.summary: A Supertrend cross arms a setup, and the signal waits until price breaks a volatility range beyond the crossing close while the ATR is rising.
sideways-market-skipper-scanner.descriptionHtml:
This setup is built to skip the sideways drift that often follows a Supertrend flip. A Supertrend line (an ATR band around the bar's midpoint that only tightens while the trend holds) is drawn in green below price in an uptrend and in red above price in a downtrend, with the area between it and the candle body shaded. When the close crosses the Supertrend, the setup is armed and a volatility range is projected from the crossing close: by default 1.5 times the range ATR above the close after an upward cross, or below it after a downward cross. Type Points replaces the ATR distance with a fixed number of points.

The range ATR is the chosen average (RMA, SMA, EMA or WMA) of the true range, and it is compared with its own simple average. A long signal fires on the first bullish candle that closes above the top of the range while this ATR is above its average, and a short signal on the first bearish candle that closes below the bottom of the range under the same condition. Each armed setup fires at most once, and the next cross arms a new one.

Optional filters can make the signal candle meet more conditions: a minimum bar range against a separate ATR (on by default), a minimum body share of the candle, a candle larger than the previous one, volume above its average, relative volume above its own average, a cumulative daily price change, a cumulative daily volume change against the previous day, and a time window. The table on the newest bar shows the day's cumulative percentage change, the change in cumulative volume against the previous day, and both days' cumulative volume in lakhs (units of 100,000).
sideways-market-skipper-scanner.howToReadHtml:
A candle painted light green or light red marks a Supertrend cross, the bar that arms the setup. The green step line above price (or the red one below it) is the range the market has to clear; the signal is not taken while price stays inside it. A small triangle below a light green candle is a long signal and a triangle above a light red candle is a short one. The ATR and its average are drawn on the left scale: a signal only appears while the ATR line is above its average, which means volatility is expanding.

The cross and the signal are only taken on a closed bar, so neither appears and then vanishes on a forming bar. The signal comes after the cross and after the range break, so it gives up the early part of a move in exchange for skipping many flips that go nowhere. When no candle leaves the range before the next cross, the setup simply produces no signal. The cumulative daily figures restart at midnight in the chart's timezone, and the first day on the chart has no volume figures because the running total only starts at the first change of day.

settings.label: ATR Length
settings.html: The number of bars in the ATR behind the Supertrend band. A longer length makes the band steadier and the crosses rarer.

settings.label: Factor
settings.html: How many ATRs the Supertrend band sits from the bar's midpoint. A larger factor gives fewer, later crosses.

settings.label: Display
settings.html: Draw the top and bottom of the volatility range. The signal logic runs either way.

settings.label: Range Type
settings.html: Auto ATR sets the range distance from the range ATR times its multiplier, so it rescales with the instrument. Type Points uses the fixed distance below.

settings.label: Type Points
settings.html: The fixed range distance in price points, used only when Range Type is Type Points.

settings.label: Range ATR Length
settings.html: The number of bars in the average of the true range that sets the range distance and the volatility test.

settings.label: ATR Smoothing
settings.html: The average applied to the true range: RMA, SMA, EMA (seeded with the simple mean of its first window) or WMA.

settings.label: ATR Multiplier
settings.html: How many range ATRs the range extends beyond the crossing close in Auto ATR mode. A larger multiplier asks for a bigger break.

settings.label: ATR SMA Length
settings.html: The length of the simple average of the range ATR. A signal needs the ATR above this average.

settings.label: Display ATR and ATR SMA
settings.html: Draw the range ATR and its average on the left scale.

settings.label: Apply % Change Filter
settings.html: Require the day's cumulative percentage change to be above the threshold for a long signal and below its negative for a short one.

settings.label: % Change Above/Below +/-
settings.html: The cumulative daily percentage change the price change filter asks for.

settings.label: Apply Volume % Change Filter
settings.html: Require the day's cumulative volume to be up on the previous day's total by at least the threshold.

settings.label: Volume % Change Above
settings.html: The minimum percentage change of the day's cumulative volume against the previous day. Zero only asks for no fall.

settings.label: Apply ATR Filter
settings.html: Require the signal candle's high to low range to be larger than the filter ATR times its multiplier. On by default.

settings.label: Filter ATR Length
settings.html: The number of bars in the ATR used by the ATR filter.

settings.label: Filter ATR Multiplier
settings.html: How many filter ATRs the signal candle's range must exceed. A higher value keeps only larger candles.

settings.label: Apply Body % Filter
settings.html: Require the candle body to cover at least the given share of the candle's range.

settings.label: Body % Above
settings.html: The minimum body share, in percent, for the body filter and the body size filter.

settings.label: Apply Body Size Filter
settings.html: Require the candle to pass the body share test and to be at least the given multiple of the previous candle's range.

settings.label: Body Size Multiplier (x)
settings.html: How many times the previous candle's range the signal candle's range must reach.

settings.label: Apply Volume Filter
settings.html: Require the signal candle's volume to be above the simple average of volume.

settings.label: Volume SMA Length
settings.html: The number of bars in the volume average used by the volume filter.

settings.label: Apply Relative Volume Filter
settings.html: Require relative volume (this bar's volume over the previous bar's volume average) to be above its own average times the multiplier.

settings.label: Relative Volume Length
settings.html: The length of both the volume average behind relative volume and the average of relative volume itself.

settings.label: Rel Vol SMA Multiplier
settings.html: How many times its own average the relative volume must reach.

settings.label: Apply Time Filter
settings.html: Keep signals only on bars that open inside the time window below, read in the chart's timezone.

settings.label: Time From (hour)
settings.html: The hour the time window opens.

settings.label: Time From (minute)
settings.html: The minute the time window opens.

settings.label: Time To (hour)
settings.html: The hour the time window closes. The closing minute itself is outside the window.

settings.label: Time To (minute)
settings.html: The minute the time window closes.

settings.label: Display Table
settings.html: Show the readout of the day's cumulative change and volume on the newest bar.

settings.label: Position
settings.html: Where the readout sits. The left positions use the left corners and the right and center positions use the right corners; bottom positions use the bottom corners and the rest the top.

settings.label: Size
settings.html: The text size the readout asks for. The grid is drawn at the chart's own text size, so this setting has no effect.

faq.q: Why did a Supertrend cross not produce a signal?
faq.html: A cross only arms the setup. The signal needs a candle in the new direction that closes beyond the volatility range while the range ATR is above its average and every enabled filter passes. If price stays inside the range until the next cross, no signal is given for that cross.

faq.q: Why does a new range line appear one bar after the cross?
faq.html: A range level is drawn once it has held for a bar, and it is then drawn back to the bar it was set on. On the cross bar itself the level is new, so it appears as soon as the next bar confirms it.

faq.q: Why are the volume figures in the table missing at first?
faq.html: The daily volume total only starts at the first change of day on the chart, so on the first day Vol, Vol %Chg and PD Vol all read a dash and the volume % change filter cannot pass. On the second day there is still no complete previous day: PD Vol reads a dash and Vol %Chg compares the day with itself, so it reads 0 %. From the third day every figure is filled. The volume average and relative volume filters do not use these daily totals.

faq.q: What is the difference between Auto ATR and Type Points?
faq.html: Auto ATR sets the range distance from the range ATR times its multiplier on the cross bar, so it adapts to how much the instrument is moving. Type Points uses the same fixed number of price points on every cross, which suits an instrument whose typical move you already know.

sideways-market-skipper.title: Sideways Market Skipper
sideways-market-skipper.summary: Waits out the sideways stretch after a Supertrend cross and signals only when the close breaks a volatility range set from the crossing bar.
sideways-market-skipper.descriptionHtml:
A Supertrend cross can be followed by a stretch of sideways trading. This study adds a second step that waits for price to leave it. When the close crosses the Supertrend line (from the ATR length and factor in the settings), it opens a volatility range: for an upward cross a level above the crossing close, for a downward cross a level below it. The distance is the range ATR times its multiplier, or a fixed number of points with the Type Points option.

The range ATR is the true range smoothed by RMA, SMA, EMA or WMA, and the study plots it in its own pane with its simple average. A long signal needs the close to break above the top of the range on a candle that closes above its open while the range ATR is above its average, so volatility is expanding. A short signal is the mirror image below the bottom of the range. Each cross arms one setup and the first qualifying break fires it.

Optional filters can be added to the break: the day's cumulative percentage change, the day's volume against the previous day's, a candle range wider than the ATR (on by default), a minimum body share, a candle larger than the previous one, volume above its average, relative volume above a multiple of its own average, and a time window. The Supertrend and the range levels are drawn on the price chart, the ATR pair in the study's pane.
sideways-market-skipper.howToReadHtml:
Candles coloured at a Supertrend cross show where a new range was opened, and the step line beside price is the level the market has to clear. While price stays inside the range the study does nothing, which is the sideways phase it is meant to skip. A green triangle below a candle is a long break and a red triangle above one is a short break, and those candles are coloured too.

In the lower pane, the blue ATR above the orange ATR SMA means ranges are widening, which the break requires. A signal is a description of the bar that broke out, not a forecast: a break can still fail, and on a fast chart many ranges are opened and never broken. The table reads the newest bar: %Chg is the sum of the bar-to-bar percentage changes of the close since the day began, Vol %Chg compares the day's running volume with the previous day's total, and Vol and PD Vol are those two volumes in lakhs.

settings.label: ATR Length
settings.html: The number of bars in the ATR that sets the Supertrend's distance from price.

settings.label: Factor
settings.html: How many ATRs the Supertrend sits from price. Higher values cross less often.

settings.label: Display
settings.html: Draw the top and bottom range levels on the price chart.

settings.label: Range Type
settings.html: Auto ATR sets the range width from the range ATR; Type Points uses the fixed number of points below.

settings.label: Type Points
settings.html: The range width in price points, used only when Range Type is Type Points.

settings.label: Range ATR Length
settings.html: The number of bars the true range is smoothed over for the range ATR plotted in the pane.

settings.label: ATR Smoothing
settings.html: How the true range is averaged: RMA, SMA, EMA or WMA.

settings.label: ATR Multiplier
settings.html: How many range ATRs the range level sits from the crossing close in Auto ATR mode.

settings.label: ATR SMA Length
settings.html: The length of the simple average of the range ATR; a break needs the ATR above it.

settings.label: Apply % Change Filter
settings.html: Require the day's cumulative percentage change to be above the figure for a long and below its negative for a short.

settings.label: % Change Above/Below +/-
settings.html: The day's percentage change the filter above requires.

settings.label: Apply Volume % Change Filter
settings.html: Require today's cumulative volume to beat the previous day's by at least the percentage below.

settings.label: Volume % Change Above
settings.html: The volume increase over the previous day the filter above requires, in percent.

settings.label: Apply ATR Filter
settings.html: Require the breakout candle's high-low range to exceed the filter ATR times its multiplier.

settings.label: Filter ATR Length
settings.html: The number of bars in the ATR the candle filter compares against.

settings.label: Filter ATR Multiplier
settings.html: How many filter ATRs the breakout candle's range must exceed.

settings.label: Apply Body % Filter
settings.html: Require the candle's body to cover at least the share of its range set below.

settings.label: Body % Above
settings.html: The body share, in percent of the candle's range, used by both body filters.

settings.label: Apply Body Size Filter
settings.html: Require a strong body and a range at least the multiplier times the previous candle's range.

settings.label: Body Size Multiplier (x)
settings.html: How many times the previous candle's range the breakout candle must span, as a whole number.

settings.label: Apply Volume Filter
settings.html: Require the candle's volume to be above its simple average.

settings.label: Volume SMA Length
settings.html: The number of bars in the volume average the volume filter uses.

settings.label: Apply Relative Volume Filter
settings.html: Require relative volume, this bar's volume over the previous bar's average, to beat a multiple of its own average.

settings.label: Relative Volume Length
settings.html: The number of bars in both averages behind relative volume.

settings.label: Rel Vol SMA Multiplier
settings.html: How many times its own average relative volume must reach.

settings.label: Apply Time Filter
settings.html: Allow signals only between the from and to times of each day, on the chart's clock.

settings.label: Time From (hour)
settings.html: The hour the signal window opens.

settings.label: Time From (minute)
settings.html: The minute the signal window opens.

settings.label: Time To (hour)
settings.html: The hour the signal window closes; a bar at that exact time is outside it.

settings.label: Time To (minute)
settings.html: The minute the signal window closes.

settings.label: Display Table
settings.html: Show the table of the day's percentage change and volume.

settings.label: Position
settings.html: Where the table sits; each position is drawn in its nearest corner of the chart.

settings.label: Size
settings.html: Text size of the table. Tables in this version draw at the chart's own text size, so this has no visible effect.

faq.q: Why are some Supertrend crosses not followed by a signal?
faq.html: A cross only arms the setup. The signal needs a later close beyond the range level on a candle in the same direction, with the range ATR above its average and every switched-on filter passing. If price stays inside the range, or the opposite cross comes first, there is no signal.

faq.q: Where does a range line start and stop?
faq.html: The level is fixed on the crossing bar and drawn only on bars where it is unchanged from the bar before, shifted one bar back. So the step starts on the crossing bar, and the last bar before the next cross is left blank, which leaves a one-bar gap between two ranges.

faq.q: Should I use Auto ATR or Type Points?
faq.html: Auto ATR follows the instrument's own volatility, so the same settings scale to any symbol and timeframe. Type Points is a fixed distance and only makes sense once you know what a typical move is for the one instrument you trade.

faq.q: Why can Vol or PD Vol read n/a?
faq.html: The day's volume is a running total that starts on the first new day the chart reaches, so the partial day the chart opens on has none. On that first full day PD Vol is n/a, because the day before it had no total, and Vol %Chg reads 0.00 %. From the second full day on, both volumes are filled.
